# 

1. #  **Introduction** {#introduction}

   1. ## **Overview of the project** {#overview-of-the-project}

As online education continues to grow rapidly, the demand for learning natural sciences — particularly astronomy — in a visual, interactive, and engaging manner has become increasingly critical. However, most e-learning platforms available in Vietnam today only deliver content through static text or passive video, failing to leverage the potential of 3D graphics technology and artificial intelligence in education. Moreover, high-quality astronomy learning resources are predominantly written in English, creating a significant barrier for the majority of Vietnamese students and learners.

Concepts such as geologic time, planetary orbits, and biological evolution are highly abstract when approached solely through theory. Interactive 3D simulation is the most effective method for learners to comprehend the vast scales of space and time that traditional textbooks cannot adequately convey. At the same time, with the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), integrating AI into learning management systems is no longer a luxury — it has become a necessity for personalizing learning experiences and improving instructional effectiveness.

Motivated by these realities, the project "**Research and Development of an Integrated Time-Based Astronomy Education System with Simulation**" was developed to build a comprehensive learning system in which users can not only read and listen, but also directly interact with scientifically accurate 3D simulations (drawing from over 500,000 fossil records from the Paleobiology Database and real orbital data from NASA JPL), receive support from a context-aware AI Tutor (which understands which lesson the user is studying and which page they are on), and engage with a learning community featuring discussion forums and up-to-date astronomy news. The platform targets secondary and high school students, university students, self-learners, and educators in Vietnam, and is deployed across multiple platforms (web, PWA, Android) with Vietnamese as the primary UI language.

2. ## **Purpose of the project** {#purpose-of-the-project}

The main objective of this study is to design and develop an interactive online educational platform for astronomy and Earth science that not only provides structured learning content but also integrates immersive 3D simulations and an intelligent AI-powered tutoring assistant to enhance the learning experience. The system aims to combine the functionalities of a modern e-learning platform with advanced technologies in visualization, artificial intelligence, and real-time data interaction in order to create an engaging, reliable, and accessible solution for science education.

The overall objective is to build a prototype platform for astronomy and Earth history education that ensures scientific accuracy, interactivity, and personalization, while simultaneously offering 24/7 learner support through an AI tutor powered by Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). By doing so, the project contributes to improving the quality of online science education and strengthening learner engagement through the integration of digital technology into the academic environment.

The specific objectives include:

* Designing a user-friendly web interface that allows learners to search, browse, and enroll in astronomy and Earth science courses, as well as explore free-access tutorials and structured learning paths with ease.  
* Developing an interactive 3D simulation module — including an Earth History Simulator, a Solar System scene, and a Milky Way visualization — that enables learners to explore scientific phenomena across geological time and astronomical scale in a visually immersive environment.  
* Integrating an AI Tutor based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and natural language processing to provide real-time support, such as answering domain-specific questions, guiding learners through course content, and proactively navigating users to relevant lessons or simulations based on conversational context.  
* Building a content authoring system (Studio) that enables teachers to create and publish rich, multimedia lessons using a block-based editor supporting text, images, video, mathematical notation, interactive charts, quizzes, and embedded 3D models.  
* Ensuring data security and privacy for all users, as well as implementing role-based access control for students, teachers, moderators, and administrators in accordance with the platform's operational requirements.  
* Conducting testing and evaluation of the system's performance to identify strengths, limitations, and directions for future improvement.

  3. ## **Object and scope of the research** {#object-and-scope-of-the-research}

     1. ### **The object of the research** {#the-object-of-the-research}

* Study interactive online learning methods in the fields of astronomy and Earth science, including course and content management processes, structured learning path design, learner progress tracking, and optimization of the overall educational experience.  
* Analyze user needs and behaviors across different stakeholder groups — students seeking accessible and engaging science content, teachers requiring efficient content authoring tools, and administrators managing platform operations — in order to design a system that meets the practical demands of each role.  
* Research the integration of an AI-powered tutoring assistant based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide 24/7 personalized support, answer domain-specific questions about astronomy and Earth history, guide learners through course materials, and proactively navigate users to relevant lessons or simulations based on conversational context.  
* Explore the application of 3D visualization technologies to scientific education, including the use of React Three Fiber and Three.js to develop an Earth History Simulator, a Solar System scene, and a Milky Way visualization that allow learners to explore scientific phenomena in an immersive and interactive environment.  
* Investigate suitable technologies for system development, including Next.js 14 for the Frontend, Node.js with Express.js for the Backend API, Python FastAPI for AI and embedding services, MongoDB for database management, and the BGE-M3 multilingual model for natural language understanding in the RAG pipeline.

  2. ### **The scope of the research** {#the-scope-of-the-research}

* Focus on developing the core functionalities of the educational platform, including user registration, login, role-based access control, course browsing and enrollment, lesson viewing with multimedia content blocks, quiz participation, learning progress tracking, and community forum interaction.  
* Integrate an AI Tutor capable of handling learner requests such as answering subject-specific questions, providing guidance through course content, processing image-based queries, and using agent tools to navigate users to relevant lessons or the Earth History Simulator.  
* Limit the system to a prototype scope, without extending to full-scale commercial deployment, integration with official national education management systems, or advanced content certification and accreditation processes.  
* Include a payment integration with VNPay to support paid course enrollment, while limiting financial features to basic transaction processing and order management, without extending to complex subscription models or third-party financial reporting systems.  
* Target user groups including individual learners with an interest in astronomy and natural sciences, educators and content creators seeking to develop and publish structured online courses, and platform administrators responsible for system governance and quality assurance.

  4. ## **Research methods**	 {#research-methods}

The research is carried out through a combination of theoretical study and practical implementation. First, relevant literature and previous studies on e-learning systems, educational technology, 3D scientific visualization, and AI-powered tutoring systems are reviewed to establish the theoretical foundation. This step provides an understanding of the challenges and requirements in building an interactive educational platform for astronomy and Earth science, as well as the technical considerations involved in integrating a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline and real-time 3D simulations into a web-based learning environment.

Following the theoretical study, the project applies a system development approach that includes requirement analysis, system design, implementation, and evaluation. Requirement analysis is conducted to identify the needs of different user groups, including students seeking interactive and personalized learning experiences, teachers requiring a capable content authoring environment, and administrators needing comprehensive management tools. Based on these requirements, the system is designed with a focus on usability, modularity, and cross-platform accessibility. The implementation phase involves developing the web application using Next.js 14 for the frontend, Node.js with Express.js for the backend API, Python FastAPI for AI and embedding services, and MongoDB for database management. In addition, React Three Fiber and Three.js are applied to develop the 3D simulation modules, while the BGE-M3 multilingual model and a curated knowledge corpus are used to build the RAG-based AI Tutor.

Finally, the system is tested through functional verification and user evaluation. The testing phase focuses on assessing the performance of core features such as user registration and authentication, course browsing and enrollment, lesson content rendering, quiz functionality, 3D simulation interaction, AI Tutor response accuracy, community forum operations, and payment processing via VNPay. The outcomes of the tests are analyzed to identify strengths, limitations, and potential improvements for future development.

5. ## **Expected results to be achieved** {#expected-results-to-be-achieved}

* Successfully develop an interactive online educational platform for astronomy and Earth science with core functionalities such as user registration, login, role-based account management, course browsing and enrollment, structured lesson viewing with multimedia content, quiz participation, learning progress tracking, and community forum interaction.  
* Deliver an immersive 3D simulation module including an Earth History Simulator — featuring a navigable geological timeline spanning 4.6 billion years and geographically distributed fossil occurrence data — alongside a Solar System scene and a Milky Way visualization, enabling learners to explore scientific concepts in a visually engaging and interactive environment.  
* Integrate an AI Tutor powered by Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) that is capable of providing 24/7 personalized learning support, answering domain-specific questions about astronomy and Earth science, processing both text and image inputs, and proactively guiding learners to relevant lessons or simulations through intelligent agent tools.  
* Provide a content authoring environment (Studio) that enables teachers to independently create, edit, and publish structured courses and learning paths using a rich block-based editor supporting diverse content types such as text, images, video, mathematical notation, interactive charts, quizzes, and embedded 3D models.

* Provide a user-friendly and visually compelling interface that enhances the online learning experience, increases learner engagement with science education, and demonstrates the potential of combining 3D visualization and artificial intelligence in building next-generation educational platforms.

2. # **Literature review** {#literature-review}

   1. ## **Next.js** {#next.js}

Next.js is an open-source React-based web framework developed and maintained by Vercel. It extends React's capabilities by providing built-in support for server-side rendering (SSR), static site generation (SSG), and the App Router architecture introduced in version 13 and stabilized in version 14\. Next.js follows a file-based routing convention, where each file inside the app/ directory automatically becomes a route, and supports React Server Components — allowing parts of the UI to be rendered on the server without sending unnecessary JavaScript to the client.

**Why choose Next.js?**

Next.js was chosen as the primary frontend framework due to its powerful rendering strategies, developer experience, and suitability for building a data-rich educational platform. Specifically:

* Server-Side Rendering and Performance: Next.js renders pages on the server before delivering them to the browser, significantly reducing initial load time. This is particularly important for the landing page and course listing pages, where SEO visibility and fast content delivery directly impact user engagement.  
* App Router and Layouts: The App Router enables shared layouts across nested routes, making it straightforward to implement persistent UI elements such as the main navigation header, the AI Tutor sidebar, and the mobile bottom navigation across all pages without redundant re-renders.  
* React Server Components: Allows data fetching to occur on the server before the page is sent to the client, eliminating unnecessary API round-trips and reducing client-side JavaScript bundle size, which benefits performance on low-end devices.  
* Ecosystem Integration: Next.js integrates natively with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and third-party authentication providers, and supports Capacitor for packaging the web application as an Android mobile app.  
* Project Suitability: Next.js is well-suited for a platform that combines both public-facing pages (landing page, course catalog) and protected, dynamic pages (course viewer, studio editor, admin dashboard), providing the flexibility to apply different rendering strategies per route as needed.

  2. ## **Three.js and React Three Fiber** {#three.js-and-react-three-fiber}

Three.js is an open-source JavaScript library that provides a high-level abstraction over WebGL, enabling developers to create and display 3D graphics in web browsers without requiring direct interaction with the low-level WebGL API. It provides built-in support for geometries, materials, lights, cameras, textures, and animation loops. React Three Fiber (R3F) is a React renderer for Three.js, allowing Three.js scenes to be composed declaratively using React components and hooks, and integrating naturally with React's component lifecycle and state management.

**Why choose Three.js and React Three Fiber?**

Three.js and React Three Fiber were selected as the 3D rendering technologies for the platform's simulation modules due to their power, flexibility, and deep integration with the React ecosystem. Specifically:

* WebGL Abstraction: Three.js abstracts the complexity of raw WebGL programming, allowing the development of sophisticated 3D scenes — such as a textured rotating Earth globe, instanced fossil point clouds, a full Solar System with orbital mechanics, and a Milky Way visualization — without requiring low-level GPU programming knowledge.  
* Declarative Scene Composition: React Three Fiber allows 3D scenes to be built using familiar React component patterns, enabling the team to manage scene objects, cameras, lights, and animations in a structured and maintainable way that is consistent with the rest of the application codebase.  
* Performance Optimization: Features such as instanced meshes (used for rendering thousands of fossil occurrence points on the globe simultaneously) and requestAnimationFrame-based animation loops ensure smooth, high-performance rendering even for complex scientific visualizations.  
* Texture and Material Support: Three.js supports high-resolution texture mapping, which is essential for the Earth History Simulator — where the globe's appearance (continental configuration, ocean coverage, vegetation) changes dynamically based on the selected geological time period.  
* Project Suitability: The interactive Earth History Simulator, Solar System Cockpit, and Milky Way scene are the most distinctive features of the platform, and React Three Fiber provides the ideal bridge between the complexity of 3D rendering and the component-driven architecture of the frontend.

  3. ## **Node.js** {#node.js}

Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform runtime environment for JavaScript built on Google Chrome's V8 engine. It enables JavaScript to be executed on the server side, extending the language beyond its traditional browser-only context. Node.js adopts an event-driven, non-blocking I/O model, making it highly efficient for handling large numbers of concurrent connections, which is particularly valuable for web servers, RESTful APIs, and real-time applications.

**Why choose Node.js?**

Node.js was selected as the backend runtime environment for the main API service due to its performance characteristics and compatibility with the overall JavaScript-based technology stack. Specifically:

* Unified JavaScript Stack: Using JavaScript across both the frontend (Next.js) and backend (Node.js) reduces the cognitive overhead for the development team, enables sharing of data validation logic and TypeScript type definitions between services, and accelerates full-stack development.  
* High Concurrency Handling: The event-driven, non-blocking I/O model allows the API server to handle multiple concurrent requests efficiently — such as simultaneous course enrollment operations, forum post submissions, and media uploads — without blocking the main execution thread.  
* Rich Ecosystem via NPM: Access to a vast library of packages enables rapid integration of essential features, including JWT-based authentication, bcrypt password hashing, Multer for file upload handling, and Mongoose for MongoDB object modeling.  
* Project Suitability: Node.js serves as the foundation for the main Express.js API (port 3002), which acts as the central hub for all business logic related to courses, users, payments, community, and administration, and integrates seamlessly with MongoDB as the primary database.

  4. ## **Express.js** {#express.js}

Express.js, commonly referred to as Express, is a minimalist and flexible web application framework built on top of Node.js. It provides a thin layer of fundamental tools for building web applications and RESTful APIs, including routing, middleware chaining, request and response handling, and error management. Unlike opinionated frameworks, Express imposes no rigid project structure, giving developers full control over application architecture while significantly reducing the boilerplate required to build an HTTP server.

**Why choose Express.js?**

Express.js was selected to handle server-side routing and business logic for the platform's unified API service, offering a balance between simplicity and extensibility. Specifically:

* Modular Monolith Architecture: Express's flexible routing system allows the API to be organized into distinct feature domains — authentication, courses, community, payment, media, and administration — each mounted as an independent router on a single Express application, providing clear module boundaries while maintaining a unified deployment.  
* Middleware Flexibility: Express supports a composable middleware pipeline, enabling the straightforward application of shared concerns such as JWT authentication, role-based authorization, request logging, error handling, and CORS configuration across all routes with minimal code duplication.  
* RESTful API Development: Express provides a clean and expressive API for defining RESTful endpoints, making it straightforward to implement CRUD operations for entities such as courses, lessons, enrollments, forum posts, and orders.  
* Project Suitability: Express integrates natively with Mongoose for MongoDB interaction, enabling efficient implementation of complex data operations such as enrollment management, learning progress tracking, and payment order fulfillment within a single, cohesive API service.

  5. ## **MongoDB** {#mongodb}

MongoDB is an open-source, document-oriented NoSQL database that stores data in BSON (Binary JSON) format rather than in relational tables as in traditional SQL databases. It organizes data into collections of documents, where each document can have a flexible, schema-less structure that allows fields to vary between documents within the same collection. MongoDB is particularly well-suited for applications that handle complex, hierarchical, or frequently evolving data structures, and provides powerful querying, aggregation, and indexing capabilities.

**Why choose MongoDB?**

MongoDB was chosen as the primary database for the platform due to its flexibility in modeling complex educational content and its seamless integration with the JavaScript-based technology stack. Specifically:

* Flexible Document Schema: The schema-less nature of MongoDB allows lesson content to be modeled as an array of heterogeneous blocks — each block having a different structure depending on its type (richtext, image, video, math, chart, slider, 3D model embed, etc.) — without requiring complex relational joins or schema migrations when new content types are introduced.  
* Hierarchical Data Modeling: MongoDB's document model naturally represents nested structures such as courses containing modules, modules containing lessons, and lessons containing sections and quiz questions, all within a single document, reducing query complexity and improving read performance.  
* Aggregation Pipeline: MongoDB's aggregation framework supports complex analytics queries required by the admin dashboard, such as enrollment statistics, payment revenue summaries, and learning progress reports, without requiring a separate analytics database.  
* Integration with Mongoose: The Mongoose ODM (Object Document Mapper) for Node.js provides schema validation, middleware hooks (such as pre-save password hashing), and a clean query API that improves developer productivity and data integrity across all collections.  
* Project Suitability: MongoDB is ideal for managing the platform's diverse data entities — including Users, Courses, Enrollments, Tutorials, Learning Paths, Forum Posts, Comments, Orders, and Earth History Stages — each with distinct and complex structures that benefit from the flexibility of document-based storage.

2. ## **System requirements** {#system-requirements-1}

*Table 2: System requirements*

| No | System Requirement | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Authentication Methods | JWT-based authentication with access tokens stored in localStorage. Firebase OAuth 2.0 for Google and Facebook social login. |
| 2 | Password Security | Passwords hashed using bcryptjs with salt rounds before storing in database. Token-based password reset flow via email verification link. |
| 3 | API Architecture | RESTful API built with Express.js. JSON responses with standard HTTP status codes. Modular monolith structure with feature-based routing domains. |
| 4 | Authorization & Roles | Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with four roles: student, teacher, moderator, and admin. Route protection enforced via authMiddleware and requireRole() middleware. |
| 5 | 3D Rendering Engine | Three.js with React Three Fiber for declarative 3D scene composition. Supports textured globe rendering, instanced mesh fossil points, orbital animations, and dynamic texture swapping based on geological stage. |
| 6 | AI Tutor Integration | RAG-based AI assistant powered by BGE-M3 multilingual embedding model and a curated knowledge corpus. Supports both text and image (multimodal) input. LLM backend switchable between OpenRouter (cloud) and LM Studio (local). |
| 7 | Agent Tools | LLM function-calling tools enable the AI Tutor to proactively navigate users within the application, including opening specific lessons (open\_lesson), switching to Earth History Simulator at a given time period (go\_to\_explore), and redirecting to platform pages. |
| 8 | Search & Filter | Text-based search for courses and tutorials by title. Filter options by difficulty level, topic category, price range (free or paid), and publication status. |
| 9 | Payment Integration | VNPay payment gateway for paid course enrollment. HMAC-SHA512 signature verification on callback to ensure transaction integrity. Order status lifecycle: pending → completed / failed. |
| 10 | Media Upload & Serving | Multer middleware for handling file uploads (images, videos) restricted to teacher and admin roles. Uploaded files served statically. Next.js rewrites /media/\* requests to the media service to avoid exposing internal ports. |

3. ## **Requirements Identification** {#requirements-identification}

   1. ### **Functional Requirements** {#functional-requirements}

- **User authentication & account management:**  
* Registration: Users can create a new account by providing their email address, display name, and password. The system validates email uniqueness before creating the account.  
* Login & Logout: Users can securely log in and log out using JWT-based authentication. Access tokens are stored in localStorage and attached to all protected API requests.  
* Social Login: Users can authenticate using their Google or Facebook account through Firebase OAuth 2.0, with automatic account creation or linking on first login.  
* Password Reset: Users can reset their forgotten password through an email verification flow. The system sends a time-limited reset link and validates the token before allowing the password change.  
* Update Profile: Users can update personal information including display name and avatar picture. Changes are validated and persisted to the database immediately.  
* Teacher Application: Users can submit an application to become a teacher on the platform. The application is reviewed and approved or rejected by an administrator.  
- **Course & lesson management:**  
* Browse Courses: Users can view the full list of published courses with information on title, thumbnail, difficulty level, and price.  
* Search & Filter Courses: Users can search for courses by keyword or filter by difficulty level and topic category.  
* View Course Details: Users can view comprehensive course information including description, module structure, lesson list, price, and enrollment status.  
* Enroll in Courses: Depends on **distribution strategy** (`self_paced` | `instructor_led` | `hybrid`). **Catalog enroll** (free: `POST /api/courses/:slug/enroll` from learn viewer; paid: UC-12 checkout) applies when `catalogEnabled !== false`. **Cohort enroll** (UC-13) is the only path for `instructor_led`; hybrid supports both catalog and cohort (upgrade checkout with `cohortId` when upgrading from catalog to a paid cohort).  
* View Lesson Content: Enrolled users can access lesson content rendered from multiple block types including rich text, images, videos, code blocks, mathematical notation (LaTeX), interactive charts, sliders, quizzes, and embedded 3D models.  
* Take Quizzes: Users can answer quiz questions embedded within lessons and receive immediate feedback indicating correct and incorrect answers.  
* Track Progress: Users can view their learning progress per course, including completed lessons and overall completion percentage, from their personal dashboard.  
- **Learning paths & tutorials:**  
* Browse Learning Paths: Users can explore structured learning paths that organize courses and concepts into a guided curriculum with defined prerequisite relationships.  
* Access Tutorials: Users can access free tutorial content without enrollment for supplementary and self-directed reference study.  
* View Concepts: Users can read definitions and explanations of key astronomical and scientific concepts linked within courses and learning paths.  
- **3D simulation & exploration:**  
* Earth History Simulator: Users can explore an interactive 3D Earth globe and navigate a geological timeline spanning 4.6 billion years. The globe's appearance changes dynamically based on the selected time period to reflect continental configuration and climate conditions.  
* Fossil Exploration: Users can view fossil occurrence data geographically distributed as points on the 3D globe, filtered automatically by the selected geological time period. Users can click on fossil groups to fly the camera to the relevant region.  
* Solar System Visualization: Users can explore a 3D Solar System scene with planetary orbits, rotation animations, and a cockpit-style interactive interface for navigating between planets.  
* Milky Way Visualization: Users can view a 3D representation of the Milky Way galaxy as part of the astronomical exploration features.  
- **AI Tutor:**  
* Text-Based Chat: Users can send text questions to the AI Tutor and receive context-aware answers grounded in the platform's curated astronomy and Earth science knowledge corpus.  
* Image Input: Users can attach an image alongside their text question and receive a multimodal response from the AI Tutor interpreting both inputs.  
* Course-Context Tutor: When accessed within a course, the AI Tutor is aware of the course structure and the current lesson being viewed, providing responses relevant to the learning context.  
* Agent Navigation: The AI Tutor can proactively suggest and execute navigation actions — such as opening a specific lesson or redirecting to the Earth History Simulator at a relevant geological time period — based on the user's conversational intent.  
- **Community & forum:**  
* Browse Forums: Users can view available forum categories and browse posts within each forum.  
* Create & Manage Posts: Authenticated users can create new discussion posts with a title and content, and manage their own posts.  
* Comment on Posts: Users can reply to posts with threaded comments, supporting nested comment structures.  
* Vote on Content: Users can upvote or downvote posts and comments to surface the most helpful community contributions.  
* Read News: Users can browse astronomy news articles published on the platform's community section.  
- **Payment & enrollment:**  
* Purchase Courses: Users can initiate payment for a paid course, which redirects them to the VNPay payment gateway to complete the transaction securely.  
* Payment Callback Processing: The system verifies the VNPay callback signature and response code upon return, then automatically grants course enrollment upon successful payment.  
* Order History: Users can view their payment order history including course name, transaction reference, amount, currency, and current order status.  
- **Teacher content authoring (Studio):**  
* Create & Edit Courses: Teachers can create new courses and edit course metadata including title, description, thumbnail, difficulty level, price, and publication status.  
* Manage Modules & Lessons: Teachers can organize course content into modules and add lessons to each module, defining lesson type as text, visualization, or quiz.  
* Block-Based Lesson Editor: Teachers can compose lesson content using a block-based editor supporting multiple block types: rich text, image, video, code, embed, 3D model, callout, divider, math (LaTeX), chart, interactive slider, and Observable notebook.  
* Upload Media: Teachers can upload image and video files to be embedded within lesson content blocks.  
* Manage Learning Paths: Teachers can design learning paths by creating content nodes, defining connections between them, and setting prerequisite relationships.  
* Manage Tutorials: Teachers can create and publish free tutorial content organized into structured sections.  
- **Admin management:**  
* User Management: Administrators can view all registered users, deactivate accounts that violate platform policies, and restore previously deactivated accounts.  
* Teacher Approval: Administrators can review pending teacher applications and approve or reject them, which updates the applicant's role accordingly.  
* Platform Analytics: Administrators can access a dashboard displaying key metrics including enrollment statistics, payment revenue summaries, and community activity reports.  
* Content Moderation: Moderators and administrators can review and manage community posts and comments to maintain platform content standards.

  2. ### **Non-Functional Requirements** {#non-functional-requirements}

* Performance: The system must deliver fast page load times by leveraging Next.js Server-Side Rendering and optimized 3D rendering techniques, ensuring a smooth and responsive experience across all core features.  
* Security: All sensitive data must be protected through password hashing with bcryptjs, JWT-based route authentication, server-side role enforcement, VNPay callback signature verification, and AI input sanitization to prevent misuse.  
* Usability: The interface must be intuitive and consistent across all user roles and screen sizes, providing clear navigation, informative feedback messages, and a responsive layout that works seamlessly on both desktop and mobile devices.  
* Scalability: The modular backend architecture and MongoDB database must support future growth in users, content, and traffic without requiring significant structural changes to the existing system.

  4. ## **Use Case Models** {#use-case-models}

     1. ### **Use Case Diagram** {#use-case-diagram}

The Cosmo Learn use case model is organized into **nine diagram pages** (draw.io): **01 Overview**, **02 Authentication & Account**, **03 Courses & Enrollment**, **04 Explore & 3D**, **05 Community**, **06 Rewards & Notifications**, **07 Studio (Teacher)**, **08 Administration**, and **09 AI Agent (Cosmo)**. The authoritative diagram source in the repository is `UC Diagram.drawio` (regenerate via `npm run diagrams:uc`). The generator script maintains **`CATALOG_UC50`**: exactly **50 ovals**, one per catalog row UC-01 … UC-50; the build fails if the diagram drifts from the catalog.

**Actors**

| Actor | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Guest** | Unauthenticated visitor: register, browse catalog, preview courses/LP/Explore, Cosmo chat (demo alternate flow). |
| **Student** | Registered learner: enroll, pay, lessons, LP, Explore, gems, community, full Cosmo agent. |
| **Teacher** | Content author; **generalizes Student** (inherits all student use cases) plus Studio. |
| **Moderator** | Community moderator: login, browse, moderate and report content. |
| **Admin** | Platform operator: **platform analytics** on `/admin` (UC-50), users (incl. send reset, deactivate/restore), orders, teacher approval, gem economy, promo/broadcast, audit/system; moderation via UC-31 (same as Moderator on admin moderation). |

**UML relationships (summary)**

| Relation | Examples |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Generalization** | Teacher → Student |
| **<<extend>>** | View Lesson → View Course; Take Quiz / Submit Assignment → View Lesson; Study LP In-Depth → View Learning Path; Contextual Quiz → Explore Sky / 3D; Concept Quiz / Rate Reply / Guest demo → Chat with Cosmo; Recall Quiz → View Lesson; First-visit Explore guide → View 3D Simulation (not a separate UC) |
| **<<include>>** | Pay Order → Enroll in Course (catalog); Pay Order + `cohortId` → cohort placement |
| **Alternate flows** | Google/Facebook OAuth on Register and Log In (not separate use cases) |

3. ### **Use Case Specification**  {#use-case-specification}

Specifications follow **catalog order by package** where possible. Each subsection title includes the **UC ID**. Tables use **`[UC-XX]`** in the first column (not the old sequential 01–29).

#### ***UC-01 Register***

| \[UC-01\] | Register |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actor** | Guest |
| **Trigger** | Guest clicks the "Register" or "Sign Up" button on the navigation header or landing page. |
| **Description** | Allows a new user to create an account on the Cosmo Learn platform by providing their email address, display name, and password. The system validates the input and creates a new student account upon success. |
| **Pre-Conditions** | 1\. The user is not currently logged in.  2\. The user has a valid email address that has not been previously registered. |
| **Post-Conditions** | 1\. A pending local account is created (`accountStatus: pending_verification`) or an existing pending registration is refreshed.  2\. After email verification (`POST /auth/register/verify-email`), the user receives a JWT and is redirected to `/onboarding` (logged in). |
| **Main Flow** | 1\. Guest navigates to the Register page (`/register`).  2\. System displays fields: Display Name, Email, Password (minimum 6 characters).  3\. Guest submits the form.  4\. System validates email format and uniqueness, hashes the password (bcrypt), and creates a pending user (`POST /auth/register`).  5\. System sends a 6-digit verification code to the email and shows the verification step.  6\. Guest enters the code; System verifies via `POST /auth/register/verify-email`, issues JWT, stores session, and redirects to `/onboarding`. |
| **Alternate Flow** | 2a. Navigate to Register via Login Page  2a.1. Guest clicks the register link on `/login`.  2a.2. Flow continues from step 2 of Main Flow.  5a. Resend verification  5a.1. Guest requests a new code via `POST /auth/register/resend-verification`.  7. OAuth (Google / Facebook)  7.1. Guest clicks **Continue with Google** or **Continue with Facebook** on Register (or Login — UC-02).  7.2. Firebase OAuth popup; Guest grants provider permissions.  7.3. Client sends Firebase ID token to `POST /auth/firebase`; backend verifies, links or creates account (`provider` / `multi`).  7.4. JWT issued; redirect `/dashboard` or `/onboarding`.  7a. Existing local account with same email — provider linked as `multi`.  7b. Guest cancels popup — no session change. |
| **Exception Flow** | 4a. Email Already Registered  4a.1. Email belongs to an active or social-only account.  4a.2. System returns an appropriate error (e.g. use Google/Facebook login).  4b. Password Too Short  4b.1. Password has fewer than 6 characters.  4b.2. System displays a validation message.  6a. Invalid or Expired Code  6a.1. Verification fails.  6a.2. Guest may resend or re-enter the code. |

#### ***UC-02 Log In / Log Out***

| \[UC-02\] | Log In / Log Out |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actor** | Guest, Student, Teacher, Moderator, Admin |
| **Trigger** | Guest clicks the "Login" button on the navigation header or is redirected to the Login page from a protected route. |
| **Description** | Allows a registered user to authenticate into the system using their email and password. Upon successful login, a JWT access token is issued and stored in localStorage. The user can also log out to clear the session. |
| **Pre-Conditions** | 1\. The user has an existing registered account. 2\. The user's account status is "active". |
| **Post-Conditions** | 1\. (Login) JWT stored; user redirected to prior URL, `/dashboard`, or `/onboarding`. 2\. (Logout) Session cleared → landing. |
| **Main Flow** | 1\. Guest navigates to the Login page. 2\. System displays the login form with fields: Email and Password. 3\. Guest enters their email and password. 4\. Guest clicks the "Login" button. 5\. System validates that both fields are filled and the email format is correct. 6\. System looks up the user record by email and verifies the password using bcryptjs. 7\. System generates a JWT access token containing the user ID and role. 8\. System stores the token in localStorage and updates the authentication state. 9\. System redirects the user to the dashboard or the originally requested page. Logout Flow: 1\. Authenticated user clicks the "Logout" option in the navigation menu. 2\. System removes the JWT token from localStorage and clears the authentication state. 3\. System redirects the user to the landing page. |
| **Alternate Flow** | 9a. Redirect After Login 9a.1. Guest was redirected to the Login page from a protected route. 9a.2. After successful login, System redirects the user back to the originally requested page instead of the default dashboard.  10. OAuth (Google / Facebook) — same steps as UC-01 alternate flow 7 (Firebase → `POST /auth/firebase` → JWT). |
| **Exception Flow** | 6a. Email Not Found 6a.1. System cannot find any account matching the provided email. 6a.2. System displays: "Invalid email or password." 6a.3. Guest re-enters credentials and resubmits. 6b. Incorrect Password 6b.1. System finds the account but bcryptjs comparison fails. 6b.2. System displays: "Invalid email or password." 6b.3. Guest re-enters credentials and resubmits. 6c. Account Deactivated 6c.1. System finds the account but its status is "deactivated". 6c.2. System displays: "Your account has been deactivated. Please contact support." 6c.3. Guest cannot proceed with login. |

#### ***UC-03 Reset Password (self-service)***

| \[UC-03\] | Reset Password |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actor** | Guest, Student |
| **Trigger** | User clicks the "Forgot Password?" link on the Login page. |
| **Description** | Allows a registered user who has forgotten their password to reset it by verifying their email address. The system sends a time-limited reset link to the provided email, which the user follows to set a new password. |
| **Pre-Conditions** | 1\. The user has an existing account registered with an email and password (not a social-only account). 2\. The SMTP email service is properly configured on the server. |
| **Post-Conditions** | 1\. The user's password is updated in the database with the new hashed value. 2\. The reset token is invalidated after use. 3\. The user is redirected to the Login page. |
| **Main Flow** | 1\. Guest clicks "Forgot Password?" on the Login page. 2\. System displays the Forgot Password page with an Email input field. 3\. Guest enters their registered email address and clicks "Send Reset Link". 4\. System validates the email format and checks whether the email exists in the database. 5\. System generates a secure, time-limited reset token and stores it (hashed) along with an expiry timestamp in the user record. 6\. System sends a password reset email containing a link with the token to the provided address. 7\. System displays: "A reset link has been sent to your email." 8\. Guest opens the email and clicks the reset link. 9\. System validates the token and checks that it has not expired. 10\. System displays the Reset Password page with fields: New Password and Confirm New Password. 11\. Guest enters and confirms their new password and clicks "Reset Password". 12\. System validates that both passwords match and meet the minimum length requirement. 13\. System hashes the new password and updates the user record, then clears the reset token. 14\. System redirects the Guest to the Login page with a success message. |
| **Alternate Flow** | 7a. Guest Does Not Receive Email 7a.1. Guest waits but does not receive the reset email. 7a.2. Guest returns to the Forgot Password page and resubmits the request. 7a.3. System generates a new token, invalidating the previous one, and resends the email. |
| **Exception Flow** | 4a. Email Not Registered 4a.1. System cannot find any account matching the provided email. 4a.2. To prevent user enumeration, System still displays: "If this email is registered, a reset link has been sent." 4a.3. No email is actually sent. 9a. Reset Token Expired 9a.1. Guest clicks the reset link after the token has expired (typically 1 hour). 9a.2. System displays: "This reset link has expired. Please request a new one." 9a.3. Guest is redirected to the Forgot Password page to submit a new request. 12a. Passwords Do Not Match 12a.1. The New Password and Confirm Password fields do not match. 12a.2. System displays: "Passwords do not match." 12a.3. Guest corrects the input and resubmits. |

#### ***UC-07 Browse & Search Courses***

| \[UC-07\] | Browse & Search Courses |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actor** | Guest, Student, Moderator, Admin |
| **Trigger** | User navigates to the Courses page from the navigation menu or clicks "Explore Courses" on the landing page. |
| **Description** | Allows visitors and authenticated users to browse the catalog of published courses and search by keyword (`GET /api/courses?q=`). No login is required; enrolled students and staff use the same catalog view. |
| **Pre-Conditions** | 1\. At least one published course exists in the system. 2\. The user does not need to be logged in. |
| **Post-Conditions** | 1\. The user is presented with a list of published catalog courses (optionally filtered by search). |
| **Main Flow** | 1\. User navigates to `/courses`. 2\. System fetches published courses via `GET /api/courses` (catalog-enabled only). 3\. System displays course cards (thumbnail, title, level, price). 4\. User types in the search bar; after a short debounce, client calls `GET /api/courses?q=` matching title or description (case-insensitive). 5\. User clicks a course card → UC-09 View Course Details (`/courses/[slug]`). |
| **Alternate Flow** | 4a. Browse Without Search 4a.1. User leaves search empty; System shows the full default list. |
| **Exception Flow** | 4a. No Courses Match Search 4a.1. API returns an empty list. 4a.2. UI shows an empty state. 2a. No Published Courses 2a.1. Catalog is empty; System shows a friendly empty state. |

| **Main Flow** | 1\. User opens `/courses/[slug]`. 2\. System loads course outline via `GET /api/courses/:slug?outline=1`. 3\. System displays title, description, thumbnail, level, price, module/lesson syllabus (titles and metadata), and instructor card. 4\. User reviews syllabus; lesson rows link to `/courses/[slug]/learn/[lessonSlug]` when preview is allowed. |

| **Exception Flow** | 2a. Course Not Found or Unpublished 2a.1. Slug invalid or course not visible to the user. 2a.2. System returns 404 / not-found UI with link back to `/courses`. |

         11) #### ***Use Case Enroll in Course (UC-11)***

| \[UC-11\] | Enroll in Course |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actor** | Student |
| **Scope** | **Catalog / self-paced access only** — not cohort placement. Cohort paths use **UC-13 Join Cohort** (and UC-12 when cohort has a fee). |
| **Trigger** | Student clicks **Ghi danh ngay** in the catalog learn viewer (`/courses/[slug]/learn/...`) for a course that allows catalog enrollment. |
| **Description** | Creates a course-level `Enrollment` (progress rows for all lessons) so the student can access catalog delivery. Applies only when the course **`catalogEnabled !== false`** (`distributionStrategy`: `self_paced` or `hybrid`). Does **not** apply to **`instructor_led`** courses (`catalogEnabled === false`) — those reject `POST …/enroll` with `catalog_disabled` and require choosing a cohort (UC-13). |
| **Pre-Conditions** | 1\. Student is logged in. 2\. Course is published. 3\. **`catalogEnabled !== false`** (catalog channel open). 4\. Student does not already have catalog `Enrollment`. 5\.  / `isPaid` — enroll API returns `requiresPayment` (handled by UC-12, not this UC). |
| **Post-Conditions** | 1\. `Enrollment` record links student ↔ course (or existing enrollment returned). 2\. Learn viewer refreshes with catalog learner access. 3\. **No** `CohortEnrollment` — joining a class remains UC-13. |
| **Main Flow** | 1\. Student opens learn viewer for a **free** catalog course without enrollment. 2\. Sidebar shows **Ghi danh ngay**. 3\. Student confirms enroll. 4\. `POST /api/courses/:slug/enroll`. 5\. Server creates `Enrollment` + per-lesson progress. 6\. Client refetches course; student continues in catalog mode (`deliveryContext.mode: catalog`). |
| **Alternate Flow** | **By distribution strategy (teacher setting in Studio):** **A. `self_paced`** — only this UC (+ UC-12 if paid); cohort UI hidden unless open cohorts exist. **B. `hybrid`** — same catalog enroll as main flow; student may later use UC-13 on `/courses/[slug]` to join a cohort (free cohort or UC-12 upgrade with catalog credit). **C. `instructor_led`** — *not applicable*; use UC-13 instead (see Exception 4c). **Paid catalog:** 3a. API returns `requiresPayment: true` → redirect `/courses/[slug]/checkout` (UC-12); on success `completeOrderAndEnroll()` creates `Enrollment`. |
| **Exception Flow** | 4a. **Already enrolled** — API returns existing enrollment; UI refreshes. 4b. **Paid catalog** — `requiresPayment`; client → UC-12. 4c. **`instructor_led` / catalog off** — `403 catalog_disabled`: *"Khóa học chỉ mở qua lớp theo kỳ"* → student must pick a cohort (**UC-13**). 4d. **Unpublished / staff-only** — 404 unless editor preview. |

         12) #### ***Use Case Pay Order / Checkout (UC-12)***

| \[UC-12\] | Pay Order (Checkout) |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actor** | Student |
| **Trigger** | Student clicks **Mua ngay** on `/courses/[slug]` or is redirected from enroll when payment is required; cohort checkout may pass `?cohortId=`. |
| **Description** | Internal demo checkout (no live third-party gateway in production path): quote with gem voucher / promo → pending `Order` → demo card confirm → enroll. Order model supports `gateway: demo | card | vnpay | momo` for future gateways. |
| **Pre-Conditions** | 1\. Student is logged in. 2\. Course is published and requires payment. 3\. Student is not already enrolled for the same purchase scope (catalog or cohort upgrade). |
| **Post-Conditions** | 1\. `Order` status becomes `completed`. 2\. `Enrollment` (and cohort placement if applicable) is created. 3\. Student returns to `/courses/[slug]?enrolled=1` (or owned flash). |
| **Main Flow** | 1\. Student opens `/courses/[slug]/checkout`. 2\. Client loads quote via `GET /payments/checkout-quote` (list price, gem discount, promo). 3\. Student confirms → `POST /payments/checkout` creates pending order + `txnRef`. 4\. Student enters demo card details and submits → `POST /payments/checkout/:txnRef/confirm`. 5\. Server runs `completeOrderAndEnroll()` (deduct gem voucher if selected). 6\. Client redirects to course landing with success banner. |
| **Alternate Flow** | 3a. Reuse Pending Order 3a.1. Server returns an existing pending order for the same course/cohort instead of creating a duplicate. |
| **Exception Flow** | 4a. Confirm Fails / Order Expired 4a.1. Order stays or moves to `failed`; Student sees error on checkout and may retry. 2a. Already Owned 2a.1. Guard detects completed purchase; Student is redirected to course with `?owned=1`. |

System renders the lesson content by iterating through each content block and displaying the appropriate component based on block type (richtext, image, video, code, math, chart, slider, 3D model, embed, etc.). 5\. Student reads or interacts with the lesson content. 6\. System marks the lesson as visited and updates the student's learning progress. 7\. | **Post-Conditions** | 1\. Conversation is saved for signed-in users. 2\. Accepted navigation suggestions take the user to the offered screen. |

| **Alternate Flow** | 2a. Guest demo — Shorter answers and fewer actions until the user signs in. 4a. Concept quiz (UC-26) — Assistant offers an in-chat quiz on a concept. 5a. Rate reply (UC-27) — User gives thumbs up/down on a message. |
| **Exception Flow** | 3a. Policy block — Message refused when content rules fail. 4a. Service unavailable — User sees a retry message. 4b. Quiz lock — Widget is disabled until recall or exam quiz is finished. |

         25) #### ***Use Case Manage Learning Path (UC-42)***

| \[UC-42\] | Manage Learning Path |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actor** | Teacher, Admin |
| **Scope** | **Platform tutorial / learning path** (`/tutorial`, hub UC-08) — not a purchasable **Course** (UC-38/39). The teacher edits the single main path document: modules, topic **nodes**, three **depth tiers** per node, lesson items, concept links, and publish flag. **UC-43** maintains the shared concept library; this UC **uses** those concepts in lessons and may embed path-local concept copy on save. **UC-39** is course-lesson authoring only. |
| **Trigger** | Teacher or admin opens **Studio → Learning Path** (`/studio/learning-path`) from the Studio dashboard. |
| **Description** | The teacher designs the structured **Lộ trình học**: ordered **modules**, each with **nodes** (topics). Every node has three depth tracks — **Beginner (Cơ bản)**, **Explorer (Cơ chế)**, **Researcher (Sâu)** — each holding one or more **lesson items** with block-based content (same block kit as course lessons). The teacher assigns **science concepts** per lesson (with per-depth budgets), **phrase anchors** for in-text highlights, optional **Explore scene context** (showcase entity / deep-history beat), and optional **recall quiz** questions (manual or AI-assisted generation). **Topic weights** map nodes to landing topics. On save, the system normalizes content, validates concept references against the concept catalog, stores the path, and can trigger search-index refresh for the learning agent. Learners consume the published path via UC-08 and UC-20; recall quizzes at lesson end tie to UC-15. |
| **Pre-Conditions** | 1\. User is signed in as **teacher** or **admin**. 2\. Learning path record exists or can be created on first save. 3\. For concept validation, concept records exist in the catalog (UC-43) when ids are referenced. |
| **Post-Conditions** | 1\. Modules, nodes, depths, and lesson items are persisted on the main learning path. 2\. **Published** flag controls learner visibility (unpublished path returns unavailable to guests/students on public API). 3\. Invalid or unknown concept ids may be stripped or reported in the save response. 4\. Learner hub and lesson URLs reflect saved structure after publish. |
| **Main Flow** | **Open editor** — 1\. Teacher opens the Learning Path Studio screen; system loads current modules, embedded concepts snapshot, and publish state. **Structure** — 2\. Teacher adds, reorders (drag-drop), duplicates, or removes **modules**; sets module title, goals, and order. 3\. Within a module, teacher adds or edits **nodes** (topic titles, Vietnamese/English labels). 4\. Teacher configures **topic weights** on a node when linking to topic landing pages. **Lessons per depth** — 5\. Teacher selects module → node → **depth tier** → lesson item. 6\. Teacher sets lesson titles and composes **sections** in the block editor (text, media, formulas, embeds); uses **Preview** or **full lesson page** preview tabs. 7\. Teacher attaches **concept ids** to the lesson; system shows a **checklist** (budget per depth, missing anchors, prerequisite gaps between selected concepts). 8\. Teacher adds **concept anchors** (phrase + concept id) for highlighted terms in the lesson body. 9\. Optionally teacher sets **scene context** (primary Explore entity, related entities, deep-history beat) for 3D deep links from the tutorial. 10\. Optionally teacher builds or **generates** a short **recall quiz** for the lesson. **Concept prerequisites** — 11\. While editing concepts on a lesson, teacher respects **prerequisite** relationships defined on concepts (UC-43); editor warns when a selected concept requires another concept not included on that lesson. **Publish** — 12\. Teacher toggles **Published** when the path is ready for learners. 13\. Teacher saves the path. 14\. System normalizes sections and quizzes, validates concept ids, writes the learning path document, returns any invalid-id warnings, and schedules agent content reindexing. |
| **Alternate Flow** | **2a. Duplicate module/node/lesson** — Clone existing structure to speed authoring. **2b. Delete node** — Remove a topic and its depth lessons after confirmation. **7a. Over concept budget** — Editor suggests concepts to remove when depth tier exceeds recommended count (beginner / explorer / researcher limits). **10a. AI generate recall quiz** — Teacher requests auto-generated questions from lesson content; edits result before save. **12a. Unpublish** — Path hidden from public learning-path API until published again. **13a. Admin** — Same editor capabilities as teacher. |
| **Exception Flow** | **1a. Unauthorized** — Non-teacher roles redirected from Studio. **13a. Save validation** — Malformed modules array rejected. **13b. Unknown concept ids** — Stripped or listed in save response; teacher fixes references. **13c. Invalid lesson sections** — Dropped blocks counted in save feedback. **13d. Server error** — Path not saved; teacher retries. **14a. Missing path on first deploy** — Empty state until seed or first save (operational setup). |

         26) #### ***Use Case Manage Concepts (UC-43)***

| \[UC-43\] | Manage Concepts |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actor** | Teacher, Admin |
| **Scope** | **Shared concept library** for astronomy, Earth science, and related domains — not lesson layout (**UC-42**) or purchasable course content (**UC-38/39**). Each concept is a stable **id** (slug) with wiki-style fields (title, short description, full explanation, examples, related concepts, aliases, prerequisites, taxonomy, publish flag). **UC-42** attaches concept ids to learning-path lessons and validates against this catalog on save. Learners see **published** concepts in the knowledge star map, lesson highlights, Explore learning bridge, and Cosmo agent retrieval; unpublished entries remain editor-only. |
| **Trigger** | Teacher or admin opens **Studio → Concepts** (`/studio/concepts`) from the Studio dashboard. |
| **Description** | The teacher curates the platform **concept catalog** and **domain/subdomain taxonomy registry**: create and edit concept records, map prerequisites and related concepts, classify concepts by domain, review **usage** across the main learning path, clear an **unclassified queue** with bulk taxonomy assignment, and save the library. On save, the system normalizes ids and cross-references, persists concepts and taxonomy, and exposes only published concepts on the public catalog API. Deleting or unpublishing a concept does not remove lesson references automatically — **UC-42** save may strip unknown ids until the teacher fixes lessons. |
| **Pre-Conditions** | 1\. User is signed in as **teacher** or **admin**. 2\. Concept collection may be empty on first deploy; system can seed from default learning-path data when the editor first loads. 3\. For usage reporting, a learning path document exists (authored in UC-42). |
| **Post-Conditions** | 1\. Concept records and taxonomy registry are stored in the database. 2\. **Published** concepts are available to learners and downstream features; unpublished concepts are hidden from the public list. 3\. Invalid **related** or **prerequisite** links pointing to missing ids are dropped on save. 4\. Learning path editor and agent indexing can rely on the updated catalog after the next path save or reindex (operational). |
| **Main Flow** | **Open library** — 1\. Teacher opens the Concepts Studio screen; system loads all concepts (including unpublished), taxonomy registry, and scans the main learning path for **usage** (module, node, depth, lesson per concept id). **Taxonomy registry** — 2\. Teacher maintains **domains** and **subdomains** (e.g. astronomy → orbital-mechanics); new concepts must pick from this registry. **Create concept** — 3\. Teacher enters concept **id** (auto-slug), **title**, **short description**, **explanation** (required), **examples** and **related** concept ids (pipe-separated), **domain/subdomain**, **aliases**, and initial **prerequisites** from existing concepts; adds to the in-memory library. **Edit & classify** — 4\. Teacher searches/filters the concept list by id, title, content, domain, or lesson usage. 5\. Teacher expands a concept to edit fields inline, set **published**, adjust taxonomy, and tick **prerequisite** links to other concepts. 6\. For concepts missing domain/subdomain, teacher uses the **unclassified queue**: selects one or many concepts, applies suggested or chosen taxonomy, optionally with keyword-based **inference** hints. **Usage review** — 7\. Teacher reads the **usage report** per concept (which lessons reference the id) before delete or rename decisions. **Save** — 8\. Teacher clicks **Save Concept Library**; system saves the full normalized concept set and taxonomy registry in one operation and confirms success. |
| **Alternate Flow** | **3a. Duplicate id** — Create blocked with message that the id already exists. **5a. Bulk taxonomy** — Queue assigns domain/subdomain to multiple selected unclassified concepts at once. **5b. Remove from library** — Teacher deletes a concept; if the concept is used in one or more lessons, system asks for extra confirmation, then removes from the library (lesson rows may still reference the id until UC-42 is saved). **5c. Unpublish** — Teacher clears **Published** so learners no longer receive the concept on the public API while editors still see it. **8a. Admin** — Same capabilities as teacher. **8b. First-time seed** — Empty database loads default concepts from bundled seed data when the editor opens. |
| **Exception Flow** | **1a. Unauthorized** — Non-teacher roles redirected from Studio. **3b. Missing explanation** — New concept not added until explanation is filled. **8c. Save failure** — Server error; library not updated; teacher retries. **8d. Broken references after delete** — Lessons still listing removed ids are reported on next **UC-42** save (unknown ids stripped or warned). |

         27) #### ***Use Case Manage Users (UC-45)***

| \[UC-45\] | Manage User |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actor** | Admin |

| **Pre-Conditions** | 1\. The admin is logged in with role "admin". |
| **Post-Conditions** | 1\. User role, status, or other information is updated in the database as per the action taken. |
| **Main Flow** | 1\. Admin navigates to Admin Dashboard → User Management. 2\. System displays a paginated, searchable list of all registered users with columns: name, email, role, account status, and registration date. 3\. Admin searches for a specific user by name or email. 4\. Admin selects a user to view their full profile details. 5\. Admin takes one of the following actions: (a) Change Role, (b) Send Password Reset, (c) Deactivate Account, or (d) Restore Account. 6\. Restore — Admin re-enables a deactivated account. |

         28) #### ***Use Case Manage Order (UC-46)***

| \[UC-46\] | Manage Order |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actor** | Admin (scoped role with **orders** permission) |
| **Scope** | **Oversight of learner purchase orders** created by checkout (**UC-12**) — catalog paid enroll, cohort checkout, and cohort upgrade from catalog. Not course authoring (**UC-38/39**) or manual enrollment without an order (**UC-45** user detail can grant catalog access separately). Students view their own history in **UC-16**; this UC is the admin-facing list, detail, notes, cancel, and demo refund. Payment gateway in production path is **demo**; order records still carry gateway type for future VNPay/MoMo/card integration. |
| **Trigger** | Admin opens **Admin → Đơn hàng** (`/admin/orders`) from the admin shell or dashboard, optionally with a **txnRef** query to open one order. |
| **Description** | The administrator searches and filters platform **orders**, reviews buyer and course/cohort context, reads pricing breakdown (list price, promo/gem voucher discounts, amount paid), adds **internal admin notes**, cancels **pending** orders, and performs **demo refunds** on **completed** orders with optional **access revocation** (removes catalog or cohort enrollment tied to the purchase). List loads run **order maintenance** (e.g. expiring stale pending orders). Significant actions are written to the **audit log** (UC-50). Admin dashboard may show order overview stats (counts, revenue in VND) from the same order service. |
| **Pre-Conditions** | 1\. Admin is signed in with permission to manage orders. 2\. At least zero or more order records exist (created when students use UC-12 or equivalent checkout). |
| **Post-Conditions** | 1\. **Note update** — `adminNote` persisted on the order. 2\. **Cancel pending** — Order status `cancelled`; student cannot complete payment on that txnRef. 3\. **Refund (demo)** — Order status `refunded`, refund reason and timestamp stored; if revoke access is enabled, related **Enrollment** / **CohortEnrollment** rows for that purchase are removed (cohort upgrade may retain catalog enrollment per upgrade metadata). 4\. Audit entries recorded for note, cancel, and refund. |
| **Main Flow** | **Open list** — 1\. Admin opens the orders screen; system runs maintenance and returns a paginated table (buyer, course slug, txnRef, status, amount). 2\. Admin optionally filters by **status** (all, pending, completed, refunded, inactive = cancelled/failed/refunded group) and searches by **txnRef**, transaction id, course slug, or buyer email/name. 3\. Admin changes page when result set is large. **Detail** — 4\. Admin selects a row (or lands via txnRef deep link); system loads full detail: order kind (catalog / cohort / upgrade), amounts, discounts, promo code, gems committed, gateway, created/paid/expiry times, cohort title when applicable. 5\. Admin reads status and linked buyer profile (link to UC-45 user screen). **Support note** — 6\. Admin enters or edits an **admin note** and saves; system stores note and logs the update. **Resolve pending** — 7\. If status is **pending**, admin may **cancel** the order with a reason; system marks cancelled and logs action. **Resolve paid** — 8\. If status is **completed**, admin may initiate **refund (demo)**: enters a refund reason (minimum length), confirms; system marks refunded, records admin and reason, and by default revokes course/cohort access from that purchase. 9\. List refreshes to reflect the new status. |
| **Alternate Flow** | **2a. Dashboard overview** — Admin home loads aggregate order stats and recent orders without opening the full list first. **4a. Buyer drill-down** — Admin opens the purchaser’s user admin page (UC-45) from the order row. **8a. Refund without revoke** — Admin disables access revocation (API flag); enrollment remains while order shows refunded (support edge case). **8b. Cohort upgrade refund** — Revoke removes cohort enrollment; catalog enrollment may remain when purchase was an upgrade from catalog. **9a. Student view** — Learner sees the same txnRef and status in **UC-16** (read-only, no admin actions). |
| **Exception Flow** | **1a. Unauthorized** — User without orders scope redirected from admin orders. **4b. Order not found** — Invalid txnRef returns not found. **7a. Not pending** — Cancel rejected if order is already completed, cancelled, or failed. **8c. Not refundable** — Refund rejected unless status is completed. **8d. Refund reason too short** — Client blocks submit until reason is adequate. **6b / 8e. Server error** — Note or refund not saved; admin retries. |
