         30) #### ***Use Case Manage Gem Economy (UC-48)***

| \[UC-48\] | Manage Gem Economy |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actor** | Admin (scoped role with **gem** permission) |
| **Scope** | **Platform gem reward economy** — supply, earn/spend velocity, runtime tuning, shop catalogue, avatar-decoration groups, and support adjustments. **Not** learner-facing spend (**UC-33** Gem Shop, **UC-34** earn/spend) or checkout promo codes (**UC-49**). Base earn amounts (**GEM_EARN** tier 1) are defined in application code and shown **read-only** in admin; changing them requires a code release, not this UI. Runtime caps and seasonal multiplier (tier 2) and shop SKUs (tier 3) are editable here. Actions are audited (**UC-50**). |
| **Trigger** | Admin opens **Admin → Kinh tế Gem** (`/admin/gem-economy`) from the admin dashboard or shell. |
| **Description** | The administrator monitors gem **health metrics** (total balance in wallets, lifetime earned, earn/spend per day over 7d or 30d, top transaction reasons, alerts when earn outpaces spend), adjusts **runtime configuration** (seasonal earn multiplier with end date, weekly Deep History gem cap per user, maximum checkout voucher discount percent), maintains the **gem shop catalogue** (create SKUs, toggle visibility, base gem price and Vietnamese copy), manages **avatar decoration** categories (themes, banners, bulk overlay assets tied to shop items), applies **manual gem balance adjustments** to a user with mandatory reason (capped per action), and reviews **GEM_EARN** constants for alignment with product policy. Saved config and catalogue changes write to **Gem Economy audit** records. |
| **Pre-Conditions** | 1\. Admin is signed in with permission to manage the gem economy. 2\. Reward and transaction collections exist (populated as learners use UC-34 and related flows). |
| **Post-Conditions** | 1\. **Runtime config** — Validated values persisted; seasonal multiplier applies to new earn events until multiplier is 1 or end time passes. 2\. **Shop / decorations** — SKU or category rows created or updated; visibility changes affect what learners see in UC-33. 3\. **Manual adjust** — Target user `gemBalance` updated; positive adjustments may increase lifetime earned; negative adjustments do not reduce lifetime earned; a gem transaction and audit entry are recorded. 4\. Metrics refresh on next load reflect recent activity. |
| **Main Flow** | **Open console** — 1\. Admin opens the Gem Economy page; system loads metrics (selected 7d or 30d window), runtime config, shop items, and earn constants. **Metrics tab** — 2\. Admin reviews supply and velocity cards and the **top reasons** table (earn vs spend sign per reason code). 3\. If alert **HIGH_EARN_TO_SINK** appears (earn/spend ratio high), admin notes recommendation to tune seasonal multiplier, shop prices, or plan a **GEM_EARN** code change via release process. **Runtime config tab** — 4\. Admin sets **seasonal multiplier** (1–3; if above 1, sets a future **end datetime**), **weekly Deep History gem cap** (20–100), and **max voucher discount %** (0–20); adds an optional edit note. 5\. Admin saves config; server validates bounds and logs the change. **Shop catalogue tab** — 6\. Admin lists SKUs (id, Vietnamese name, category, base gem price, visible flag). 7\. Admin toggles visibility or creates a new SKU (id, name, description, category such as cosmetic/seasonal, base price, visible by default). **Avatar decorations tab** — 8\. Admin creates or edits **decoration categories** (slug, Vietnamese title/subtitle, banner image) and associates or uploads **overlay assets** for avatar-decoration shop items. **Manual adjust tab** — 9\. Admin enters target **user id**, signed **delta** (+/− gems), and **reason** (required); submits adjustment. 10\. System applies delta within per-action cap, writes transaction + audit, returns updated balance. **Constants tab** — 11\. Admin reads **GEM_EARN** map and documentation note (code-only tier). |
| **Alternate Flow** | **2a. Reload** — Admin refreshes all tabs after external learner activity. **5a. End seasonal event** — Admin sets multiplier to 1 and clears end date to stop boosted earn. **7a. Price override** — Advanced per-SKU price factors may be set via API (`itemPriceOverrides` on runtime config) within allowed band (not all fields exposed in minimal UI). **8a. Bulk overlay upload** — Admin uploads multiple decoration images into a category in one batch. **9a. Audit drill-down** — Admin opens **Nhật ký vận hành** filtered to gem source (UC-50). **10a. Negative adjust** — Balance decreases without lowering lifetime earned total (support correction). |
| **Exception Flow** | **1a. Unauthorized** — User without gem scope cannot open the page. **5b. Invalid config** — Multiplier above 1 without future end date, out-of-range cap or voucher percent, or invalid dates rejected. **7b. Duplicate SKU** — Create fails if skuId already exists. **9b. Missing user or reason** — Manual adjust rejected. **9c. Delta over cap** — Single adjustment beyond ±500 gems rejected (requires separate approval process). **9d. Zero delta** — Rejected. **5c / 7c / 9e. Server error** — Save or adjust fails; admin retries. |

         31) #### ***Use Case Promo & Broadcast (UC-49)***

| \[UC-49\] | Promo & Broadcast |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actor** | Admin (**promo** scope for coupons; **broadcast** scope for notifications) |
| **Scope** | Two related admin capabilities on separate screens: **(A) promotional codes** for paid course checkout and **(B) system broadcast notifications**. **Not** gem voucher tuning (**UC-48**) or learner notification preferences beyond receiving messages (**UC-36**). Students apply promo codes during **UC-12** checkout (one promo per order; not stacked with gem voucher). Active promos also drive **campaign banners** on course pages and related surfaces when within date and course scope. |
| **Trigger** | **(A)** Admin opens **Admin → Coupon / Mã giảm giá** (`/admin/promo-codes`). **(B)** Admin opens **Admin → Broadcast** (`/admin/broadcast`). |
| **Description** | **(A) Promo codes** — Admin creates and maintains discount coupons: code (uppercase), percent or fixed VND discount, applicability to all published courses or a selected set, optional expiry and global redemption cap, Vietnamese **banner title/body** and event key for marketing surfaces. Learners see banners when a promo is active for their course; at checkout the server validates the code (window, course scope, caps, per-user limit) and reduces the quoted price. Admin can deactivate or delete codes and toggle **active** without deleting history. **(B) Broadcast** — Admin composes a Vietnamese **title**, optional **body**, optional **href** (internal path or URL), and sends to **all active users** or to one or more **roles** (student, teacher, moderator, admin). System inserts in-app **notifications** (type admin broadcast) and pushes real-time updates where connected; recipients read them via the notification bell (**UC-36**). |
| **Pre-Conditions** | 1\. Admin is signed in with the required scope (**promo** and/or **broadcast**). 2\. For course-scoped promos, published courses exist in the catalogue. 3\. For broadcast, at least one **active** user account matches the target filter (otherwise zero recipients). |
| **Post-Conditions** | **(A)** Promo record stored; when **active** and in window, eligible learners see banners and can redeem at checkout; redemption count increments on successful **UC-12** completion. **(B)** One notification document per targeted user; UI shows recipient count after send. |
| **Main Flow** | **Promo — list & create** — 1\. Admin opens the promo codes page; system lists existing codes with status (active, scheduled, expired, disabled). 2\. Admin enters code, discount type (% or fixed VND), discount value, course scope (all courses or selected checkboxes), optional end date and usage limit, optional banner copy (defaults generated from discount). 3\. Admin submits **Create**; system normalizes code, persists promo as **active**, returns success. 4\. Admin sees confirmation that learners will see banners and can enter the code at payment. **Promo — maintain** — 5\. Admin toggles **active** off/on or deletes an obsolete code from the list. **Broadcast — send** — 6\. Admin opens the broadcast page. 7\. Admin enters title (required), body, and optional link. 8\. Admin chooses **all users** or selects target role(s). 9\. Admin submits send. 10\. System finds active users matching the filter, creates notifications in batches, pushes realtime events, and returns **recipient count**. 11\. Admin sees success message with count; form clears. |
| **Alternate Flow** | **2a. Advanced promo fields** — Admin expands optional fields: start date, max redemptions per user, accent colour, description. **3a. All courses** — Empty `courseIds` means promo applies platform-wide on paid checkout. **5a. Edit via API** — Individual fields (discount, dates, banner text) can be patched without recreating the code. **8a. Role-limited broadcast** — Only teachers receive a Studio maintenance notice, for example. **10a. Large audience** — Notifications inserted in chunks (hundreds per batch) to avoid overload. |
| **Exception Flow** | **1a. Unauthorized** — Missing promo or broadcast scope redirects from admin routes. **3b. Duplicate code** — Create rejected if code already exists. **3c. Invalid discount** — Zero, negative, or percent above 100 rejected. **3d. Selected courses empty** — Scope “selected” requires at least one course. **3e. Expiry missing** — When “has expiry” is checked without a date, create blocked. **5b. Delete not found** — Promo id invalid. **7b. Empty broadcast title** — Send blocked. **8b. No roles selected** — When not targeting all, at least one role required. **9b. Zero recipients** — Send succeeds with count 0 (no matching active users). **3f / 10c. Server error** — Create or broadcast fails; admin retries. |

         32) #### ***Use Case Platform Analytics, Audit & System (UC-50)***

| \[UC-50\] | Platform Analytics, Audit & System |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actor** | Admin (**analytics** scope for dashboard metrics; **audit** scope for operational log; **system** scope for health & jobs) |
| **Scope** | Three admin capabilities: **(1) Platform analytics** — in-app **user behaviour and business KPIs** on the admin home (`/admin`), aggregated from MongoDB (users, enrollments, orders, learning-path events, explore events, posts). **(2) Audit log** and **(3) System status** on dedicated routes. **Google Analytics (GA4)** is a **separate, optional client telemetry layer** (`NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID`): the app sends `gtag` events (page views, login, checkout started, `admin_dashboard_viewed`, etc.) to GA; the admin charts **do not** query the Google Analytics API — operators who need GA funnels open the **GA4 property** in Google’s console. Complements action logs in **UC-45**, **UC-46**, **UC-48**. Not learner **UC-36** inbox. Teacher applications on the same admin home are **UC-47**. |
| **Trigger** | **(1)** Admin opens **Admin → Tổng quan** (`/admin`) with analytics scope. **(2)** Admin opens **Nhật ký** (`/admin/audit`), optionally `?source=gem`. **(3)** Admin opens **Hệ thống** (`/admin/system`). |
| **Description** | **Platform analytics** — Admin reviews **Phân tích dữ liệu** with range **7d / 30d / 90d** and tabs: **Tổng quan** (new users, active learners, lesson completions, completion rate, trend chart for users/lessons/revenue; top courses), **Phễu** (conversion steps: signup → enroll → checkout → paid → lesson complete), **Lộ trình học** (module/depth filters, dwell and struggle signals from learning-path events), **Explore 3D** (entity views, contextual quiz attempts from explore analytics). Summary stat cards also show total users, courses, orders, pending orders, and revenue (order service when permitted). Viewing the dashboard fires a **GA4 custom event** when gtag is configured. **Audit log** — Filter by Admin / Gem economy / Security sources with paginated rows. **System status** — API, MongoDB, SMTP, news-crawl scheduler, security-event count; manual crawl trigger. |
| **Pre-Conditions** | 1\. Admin signed in with the relevant scope(s). 2\. Database reachable for aggregates and logs. 3\. For GA4 events, `NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID` is set in the client environment (otherwise in-app charts still work; GA silent). |
| **Post-Conditions** | **(1)** No analytics mutation — admin has inspected KPIs; optional GA event recorded client-side. **(2)** Audit review only. **(3)** After manual crawl, job state may update; status cards refresh. |
| **Main Flow** | **Analytics dashboard** — 1\. Admin opens `/admin`; system loads overview KPIs and top-level stats for the selected range (default 30d). 2\. Admin switches tab (**Tổng quan**, **Phễu**, **Lộ trình học**, **Explore 3D**); each tab fetches the matching admin analytics API. 3\. Admin changes **7d / 30d / 90d**; charts and funnel reload. 4\. On **Lộ trình học**, admin optionally filters by module and depth tier. 5\. Admin interprets trends (e.g. drop-off between checkout and payment) and may open deep links to **UC-46** orders, **UC-45** users, or **UC-48** gem economy. 6\. For cross-tool behaviour analysis, admin may also use **Google Analytics 4** (sessions, acquisition, custom events mirrored from the client tracker). **Audit** — 7\. Admin opens audit log, selects source, pages through actions. **System** — 8\. Admin opens system page, reads health cards; may run **crawl now** for community news. |
| **Alternate Flow** | **1a. Orders scope** — Revenue/order tiles use payment admin overview when user has **orders** scope; otherwise overview KPIs still load from analytics API. **1b. Teacher applications panel** — Same page hosts **UC-47** pending-application review without leaving `/admin`. **1c. Empty dev data** — UI shows empty-state hint when MongoDB has little activity. **2a. Funnel only** — Phễu tab loads on demand when selected. **6a. GA disabled** — No gtag; product analytics rely on in-app Mongo aggregates only. **7a. Gem filter** — `?source=gem` on audit after UC-48 adjust. **8a. Crawl skipped** — Scheduler skips if not due or disabled by env. |
| **Exception Flow** | **1d. Unauthorized** — Missing **analytics** scope hides or blocks dashboard section. **2d. Analytics API error** — Tab shows error/empty state; admin retries. **7b / 8b. Audit/system scope missing** — Cannot open `/admin/audit` or `/admin/system`. **8c. Database down** — System status shows DB failure; analytics and audit may fail. **8d. Crawl error** — Manual news crawl returns failure message. |

System renders the 3D canvas (full-viewport scene), top bar (view toggle **Hệ Mặt Trời** / **La bàn chòm sao**, optional **Hướng dẫn**, catalog control), and left **information panel** for the current focus. 3\. System opens in **showcase** mode: interactive Sun–planet–moon orbits unless the link already requested Earth history or planet deep history. **Navigate the showcase** — 4\. User rotates and zooms the scene (drag to orbit, scroll to zoom). 5\. User selects a celestial body by clicking it in 3D or choosing an entry from the **catalog** when orbits are hard to hit. 6\. System moves the camera toward the body, highlights it, and fills the panel with **Overview**, **Physics**, and **Sky** tabs (curated science copy from the content catalog where configured). 7\. User opens Earth history (panel control or link that names a geological **stage**). 9\. System switches to the Earth scene and shows the **timeline** control. 10\. User drags the timeline; the globe and era update, and **fossils** appear at configured stages. 11\. Panel text and the shareable link for the current stage stay in sync with the scrubbed time. **Planet deep history** — 12\. User opens deep history for a planet or moon (from panel when available, or from a learning-path lesson that deep-links into Explore). 13\. System loads the narrative timeline for that entity, may use an Earth-proxy scene for storytelling, and lists **learning-path lesson** links when the student is signed in. 14\. User steps through narrative beats; panel and camera follow the active beat. **Learning panel (signed-in student)** — 15\. System shows **learning steps** (read panel → contextual quiz → path lesson → ask Cosmo), **concept chips** (mastery / needs review), and quiz entry zone. 16\. User may start a contextual quiz (**UC-23**), open a linked lesson, or open Cosmo with Explore context (**UC-25**). 17\. On showcase, signed-in users may see a **progress / unlock** strip when gamification applies. **Leave or switch view** — 18\. User may switch to **La bàn chòm sao** (UC-22) via the top toggle while keeping cross-links between solar and sky topics. 19\. User leaves Explore via navigation; session preferences (e.g. tour completed) persist locally where applicable. |

Deep link from lesson or Cosmo** — Explore opens already focused on a target, Earth stage, planet-history entity, or Sky view; steps 3–7 or 8–14 start at that focus. **1b. First visit guided tour** — System auto-offers a short **Hướng dẫn** tour once per browser (or when arriving from onboarding); user can reopen it from the top bar. Tour steps adapt to showcase vs Earth vs deep history and highlight scene controls, panel tabs, learning steps, concept chips, catalog, and quiz zone. Not a separate use case. **4a. Guest** — Steps 15–17 are hidden or reduced; viewing and showcase selection still work. **6a. Panel-only study** — User reads tabs without changing 3D selection. **7a. Cross-view** — From **Sky** tab, user jumps to UC-22; returning to solar restores prior mode when possible. **16a. Concept chip** — User opens concept quiz or Cosmo from a chip (extends UC-25 / UC-26). **16b. Contextual quiz** — In-panel quiz flow per UC-23 without leaving Explore. |
| **Exception Flow** | **2a. Unsupported WebGL** — System shows a clear message that 3D Explore is unavailable on this browser/device; no silent blank canvas. **2b. Partial load** — Catalog or narrative fails while the scene still runs; panel shows retry or fallback copy, user can still navigate other entities. **5a. Invalid deep link** — Unknown target or entity resets to default showcase (or default western sky target if user forced Sky). **10a. Timeline edge** — At timeline ends, system clamps stage and keeps fossils consistent with configured bounds. **13a. Narrative unavailable** — Deep history control disabled or message shown when CMS has no story for that body. |

4. # **SYSTEM ANALYSIS AND DESIGN** {#system-analysis-and-design}

   1. ## **System architecture** {#system-architecture}

The ASTRO\_EDU (Cosmo Learn) system follows a three-layer architecture that includes the frontend, backend, database, and external service integrations. Below is the technology stack used:

* Frontend: Built with Next.js 14 (React 18\) and TypeScript – creates a responsive and interactive interface for browsing courses, exploring 3D simulations of the Solar System and Earth's history, participating in community forums, and tracking personal learning progress. The application also supports mobile platforms (iOS and Android) via Capacitor, enabling a cross-platform experience from a single codebase.

* Backend: Node.js with Express.js – manages the core logic and API services including user authentication, course management, learning progress tracking, community forums, payment processing, media file handling, gamification (Gem rewards), and real-time notifications via WebSocket.

* AI Service: Python with FastAPI – provides an intelligent tutoring chatbot powered by Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). The service retrieves relevant knowledge from an indexed educational corpus before querying the LLM, ensuring accurate and context-aware responses. It supports a multi-provider fallback chain (OpenRouter → LM Studio → Groq Cloud) to ensure high availability.

* Embedding Service: Python with FastAPI – handles text vectorization using the BAAI/bge-m3 multilingual model. It provides dense vector embeddings for both English and Vietnamese content, serving as the semantic backbone for the RAG knowledge retrieval pipeline.

* Database: MongoDB – stores all critical data including users, courses, enrollments, lessons, quizzes, assignments, forum posts, payment orders, Earth history records, fossil data (\~500,000 records from the PBDB dataset), and learning concept graphs.

* Authentication: JWT (JSON Web Token) with multiple authentication methods including email/password (with email verification), Google OAuth 2.0, and Facebook OAuth – provides secure user authentication and role-based access control across four roles: student, teacher, moderator, and admin.

* Email Service: Nodemailer – handles sending account verification emails, password reset links, order confirmation notifications, and teacher application approvals via SMTP.

* Media Storage: AWS S3 – manages course images, user profile pictures, and uploaded learning materials with CDN delivery via a configurable MEDIA\_CDN\_URL, ensuring fast and reliable asset distribution.

* Payment: Internal demo checkout on `/courses/[slug]/checkout` (pending order → demo card confirm → enroll), with gem vouchers and promo codes; order model also supports future gateways (`vnpay`, `momo`).

* Deployment: The system is hosted on Render.com (Singapore region), with the backend API and frontend web application deployed as separate services. The database is managed via MongoDB Atlas, providing scalable cloud storage with automatic backups.

![][image9]

*Figure 2:  Overall System Architecture Diagram*

The components in the ASTRO\_EDU system communicate through multiple protocols depending on the nature of the interaction:

* Client → Unified API: The frontend (web and mobile) communicates with the Unified API Service via HTTP/REST, sending JSON-formatted requests with a JWT token attached in the Authorization: Bearer header for authenticated endpoints. All business logic — including course management, payments, and community features — is handled through this channel.

* Client → Real-time Notifications: A persistent WebSocket connection (at /ws) is established between the client and the Unified API to deliver real-time event notifications such as new messages, enrollment confirmations, and system alerts without requiring the client to poll the server.

* Unified API → AI Service: When a user interacts with the AI Tutor chatbot, the Unified API (or client via proxy) sends an HTTP POST request to the AI Service (/chat). The AI Service internally retrieves relevant knowledge from its RAG index before forwarding the enriched prompt to an LLM provider.

* AI Service → Embedding Service: The AI Service communicates with the Embedding Service via internal HTTP calls (POST /embed) to convert text chunks into dense vectors during knowledge indexing and query retrieval. This connection is not exposed to the client.

* AI Service → LLM Providers: The AI Service forwards prompts to external LLM providers (OpenRouter, Groq, or LM Studio) via HTTP API calls, following a fallback chain to ensure availability if the primary provider is unreachable.

* Unified API → MongoDB: All persistent data operations are performed through Mongoose ODM over TCP, connecting to a single MongoDB database named galaxies. Only the Unified API has direct access to the database; the AI and Embedding services do not interact with it directly.

* Unified API → Third-Party Services: The Unified API integrates with external services via their respective REST APIs — Firebase Admin SDK for OAuth user verification, AWS S3 SDK for file storage, VNPay API for payment processing, and an RSS feed parser for automated astronomy news crawling.

| 8 | Email field | Textbox | User enters an email address. Field is required; the browser validates email format before submission. |
| 9 | Password field | Password Input | User enters a password of at least 6 characters. An inline error message is shown if the minimum length requirement is not met. |
| 10 | Show / Hide password toggle | Icon Toggle Button | Click → Toggles the password field between password and text input type to reveal or conceal the entered characters. |
| 11 | "SIGN UP →" button | Submit Button | Click / form submit → Calls the registration API. On success, the form transitions to the email-verification phase. On failure, an inline error message is displayed. |

6. ### **Lesson Detail Page** {#lesson-detail-page}

![][image31]

*Figure 32: Lesson Detail Page*

*Table 8: UI for Lesson Detail Page*

| No. | Name | Type | Event |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Top navigation bar | Navigation Bar | Persistent. Contains the site logo, navigation links, notification bell, and user account menu. |
| 2 | Breadcrumb trail | Navigation | Four-level trail: "Lộ trình học / \[Module\] / \[Node\] / Bài học". Each segment is a clickable link navigating to the respective level. The final segment "Bài học" is non-clickable. |
| 3 | AI Coach banner (AgentCoachBanner) | Contextual Banner | Displayed conditionally for authenticated users when the AI coach has an active nudge. Provides personalised study tips and action chips (e.g., open recall quiz, ask AI). Click dismiss → hides the banner. |
| 4 | Lesson header card | Info Card | No direct event. Displays the depth tier badge (e.g., "Cơ bản"), module indicator, lesson title, optional English subtitle, action buttons, read status badges, and the reading-progress bar. |
| 5 | Depth tier badge (e.g., "● Cơ Bản") | Badge | No event. Colour-coded chip indicating the current lesson's depth level (Beginner / Explorer / Researcher) with a gradient fill. |
| 6 | "Hỏi CosmoLearn AI" button | Action Button | Click → Opens the Cosmo AI assistant widget pre-filled with a prompt about the current lesson or the active section, if one is in view. |
| 7 | "Hỏi về bài này" button (CommunityAskButton) | Action Button | Click → Opens a community post composer pre-linked to the current module, node, and lesson context for posting a question to the forum. |
| 8 | Read status badge ("Chưa đánh dấu đọc" / "Đã đọc") | Badge | No event. Reflects the current completion state of the lesson. Changes to green "Đã đọc" when the lesson is marked complete. |
| 9 | Mastery status badge ("Chưa kiểm tra nhanh" / "Đã nắm") | Badge | No event. Displayed when a recall quiz is available. Shows amber "Chưa kiểm tra nhanh" until the quiz is passed; changes to violet "Đã nắm (mastery)" once mastered. |
| 10 | Reading progress bar | Progress Bar | No event. Automatically updated as the user scrolls through the lesson sections. Displays the percentage of content read, synced between the header card and the left sidebar. |
| 11 | Table of contents sidebar (left) | Fixed Sidebar | Visible on desktop (≥ 1024 px). Lists all lesson sections grouped by parent/child hierarchy. Click any item → Smoothly scrolls the page to that section. The active section is highlighted with a cyan left-border accent. Auto-scrolls within the sidebar to keep the active item visible. |
| 12 | Lesson content sections | Content Blocks | Each section is rendered in a rounded card. Sections containing concept-anchor terms are highlighted with cyan underlines. Hover over a highlighted term → Shows a tooltip with the concept's title and short description. Click a highlighted term → Opens the Concept Detail Panel for that concept. |
| 13 | Concept tooltip | Tooltip | Appears on mousemove over an inline concept anchor. Displays the concept title and short description. Disappears on mouseleave. Non-interactive. |
| 14 | Related community questions (LessonRelatedQuestions) | Info Section | No direct event. Displays related community questions linked to the current lesson. Clicking a question link navigates to the community post. |
| 15 | "Khái niệm trong bài" concept chip bar | Chip Group | Lists all learning concepts referenced in the lesson. Click a chip → Highlights the concept's first inline anchor in the content and opens the Concept Detail Panel for that concept. |
| 16 | "Đánh dấu đã học xong bài này" / "✓ Đã hoàn thành" button | Toggle Button | Click → Toggles the lesson's completion status. Saves locally and syncs to the backend. If a recall quiz is available and the lesson is newly marked complete, the quiz overlay opens automatically. Turns green when completed. |
| 17 | "Làm kiểm tra nhanh" / "Học xong → kiểm tra" button | Action Button | Displayed when a recall quiz is available and the lesson has not yet been mastered. Click → Opens the Recall Quiz Overlay. |
| 18 | "← Về danh sách chủ đề" button | Text Link | Click → Navigates back to /tutorial/\[moduleId\]/\[nodeId\]. |
| 19 | Previous lesson card ("← Bài trước") | Navigation Card | Displayed when a previous lesson exists in the curriculum sequence. Click → Navigates to the previous lesson's page. |
| 20 | Next lesson card ("Bài tiếp →") | Navigation Card | Displayed when a next lesson exists. If a recall quiz is pending, the card is replaced by an amber-bordered gate card showing a "Bắt đầu kiểm tra" button. Click the normal next card → Navigates to the next lesson. Click "Bắt đầu kiểm tra" → Opens the Recall Quiz Overlay. Replaced by "Về tổng quan →" at the end of the curriculum. |
| 21 | Concept Detail Panel | Slide-in Side Panel | Opens when an inline concept anchor or a concept chip is clicked. Displays the concept's full title, explanation, examples, related concepts, and cross-linked lessons. Click a related concept chip → Switches the panel to that concept. Click a related lesson link → Navigates to that lesson and closes the panel. Click "Đóng" or press Escape → Closes the panel. The panel width is resizable by dragging its left edge (desktop only). On mobile, a backdrop overlay is shown; clicking it closes the panel. |
| 22 | Recall Quiz Overlay | Modal Overlay | Opens automatically when a lesson is marked complete (if a quiz is configured) or when triggered manually. Displays multiple-choice questions. On pass → Records mastery, closes the overlay, and triggers the AI coach if configured. On fail → Optionally triggers the AI coach nudge after the overlay is closed. |

| No. | Name | Type | Event |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Top navigation bar | Navigation Bar | Persistent. Contains the site logo, navigation links, notification bell, and user account menu. |
| 2 | Enrollment success banner | Alert (Success) | Displayed when redirected back with ?enrolled=1. Shows a green confirmation message instructing the user to select a lesson. |
| 3 | Already-owned banner | Alert (Info) | Displayed when redirected with ?owned=1 and the user already has access. Informs the user they do not need to purchase again and suggests joining a cohort class instead. |
| 4 | Draft preview banner | Alert (Warning) | Displayed when the course is unpublished and viewed in preview mode. Informs the instructor that learners cannot see the course until it is published. |
| 5 | "← Danh sách khóa học" back link | Text Link | Click → Navigates back to /courses. |
| 6 | Promotional banner (CoursePromoBanner) | Banner | Displayed for unenrolled paid courses when an active promotion exists. Shows discount details and a CTA to the checkout page. |
| 7 | Course hero card | Info Card | Contains the course thumbnail, metadata strip, title, description, instructor card, and action buttons in a single unified card. |
| 8 | Course thumbnail image | Image | No event. Displayed in a 21:9 aspect-ratio container with a gradient overlay fading to the card body. Falls back to a galaxy emoji on a gradient if no thumbnail is available. |
| 9 | Metadata strip (level · weeks · lessons · price) | Informational Label | No event. Displays the course difficulty level as a rounded pill badge, optional duration in weeks, lesson count, and price in amber if the course is paid. |
| 10 | Course title | Heading | No event. Displayed in bold white at 2–3 xl font size. |
| 11 | Course description | Paragraph | No event. Full description text rendered with whitespace-pre-wrap. |
| 12 | Instructor card (CourseInstructorCard) | Info Card | No event. Displays the instructor's avatar (or initial fallback), full name, "Đã xác minh" badge (if verified), headline, organisation, expertise tags, bio (4-line clamp), years of experience, email, website link, and LinkedIn link. |
| 13 | "Vào học" button | Primary Button | Displayed for enrolled users. Click → Navigates to the first lesson at /courses/\[slug\]/learn/\[lessonSlug\]. |
| 14 | "Mua ngay · \[price\]" button | Primary Button | Displayed for unenrolled paid courses when the catalogue is open. Click → If not logged in, redirects to /login; otherwise navigates to /courses/\[slug\]/checkout. |
| 15 | "Xem trước nội dung" / "Xem nội dung khóa học" button | Secondary Button | Click → Navigates to the first lesson in preview mode. Label changes based on whether the course is paid or free. |
| 16 | "Lộ trình miễn phí" button | Secondary Button | Click → Navigates to /tutorial to access the free learning path. |
| 17 | "Hỏi cộng đồng về khóa này" button (CommunityAskButton) | Secondary Button | Click → Opens the community post composer pre-linked to this course for posting a question to the forum. |
| 18 | One-time purchase aside panel | Info Panel | Displayed for unenrolled paid courses. Shows the full price and a "Mua ngay" button. Click "Mua ngay" → Same checkout flow as item 14\. |
| 19 | Cohort-only notice banner | Alert (Warning) | Displayed when catalogOpen is false (term-based course). Informs the user to select a cohort class and register before the semester start date. |
| 20 | Cohort class section "Học theo lớp (theo kỳ)" (CourseCohortsJoin) | Interactive Section | Lists all open cohort classes for the course. Each cohort row shows the class name, start date, price, and a join/select button. Selecting a cohort and confirming → Calls the enrolment API or redirects to checkout. Displays the user's already-enrolled cohorts separately. |
| 21 | Syllabus section "Chương trình (syllabus)" | Accordion List | No direct event. Displays all course modules as expandable groups. Each module header shows the module index and title. Each lesson row shows its order number, title, description, content type label (Đọc / Video / Quiz / Bài nộp / Buổi live / 3D), and an "Mở →" link. Click "Mở →" → Navigates to /courses/\[slug\]/learn/\[lessonSlug\]. |
| 22 | Cross-sell learning path section | Info Card | No event. Displays a custom label and body text promoting the free learning path. Click "Mở lộ trình →" → Navigates to the configured tutorial href or /tutorial. |

10. ### **Explorer Page** {#explorer-page}

![][image35]

*Figure 36: Explorer Page*

*Table 12: UI for Explorer Page*

| No. | Name | Type | Event |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Top navigation bar | Navigation Bar | Persistent. Contains the site logo, navigation links, notification bell, and user account menu. |
| 2 | Gem balance chip (e.g. "46 GEM") | Status Badge | No event. Displayed for authenticated users. Shows the user's current gem balance in a cyan-bordered chamfered chip. |
| 3 | Lesson progress chip (e.g. "TIẾN ĐỘ 3/3") | Status Badge | No event. Displayed when the active entity has linked learning-path lessons. Shows how many lessons in the user's path are linked to the current entity. |
| 4 | "DANH MỤC" (Menu) toggle button | Toggle Button | Click → Opens the full entity catalogue overlay (ExploreShowcaseMenu) listing all planets & moons, dwarf planets & asteroids, comets, and spacecraft. Click again or "Close" → Dismisses the overlay. Highlighted in cyan when open. |
| 5 | "Deep History" button | Action Button | Displayed when the active entity has deep-history narrative content. Click → Switches the scene to Planet Deep History mode for the selected entity. |
| 6 | "Hóa thạch" (Fossils) button | Action Button | Displayed when the active entity supports fossil data (e.g., Earth). Click → Switches the scene to Earth History mode. |
| 7 | Entity catalogue overlay (ExploreShowcaseMenu) | Full-screen Overlay | Opens on "DANH MỤC" click. Displays four columns: Planets & Moons, Dwarf Planets & Asteroids, Comets, and Spacecraft. Hover over any item → Preloads the entity's 3D group. Click any item → Selects the entity, updates the 3D scene and left panel, and closes the overlay. |
| 8 | 3D scene canvas | Interactive 3D Viewport | Occupies the full screen. Renders orbital paths, planet/moon meshes, and lighting in real time via React Three Fiber. Click a planet or body in the scene → Selects it and updates the entity panel. Drag → Orbits the camera. Scroll → Zooms in/out. Entity labels (e.g., "EARTH", "VENUS", "MERCURY", "MARS") are rendered as 3D overlays at each body's position. |
| 9 | Entity label overlay (e.g., "EARTH", "VENUS") | 3D Scene Label | Click → Selects the entity and focuses the left panel on it. Labels remain anchored to the planet's 3D position as the camera moves. |
| 10 | Entity information panel (ShowcaseEntityPanel) | Fixed Side Panel (Left) | Displays encyclopaedic information for the active entity. Contains a header, optional tab navigation, scrollable content sections, a gamification strip, and a footer. Always visible when an entity is selected. |
| 11 | Panel header — entity group label | Label | No event. Displays the entity's group category in uppercase monospace (e.g., "HÀNH TINH · VỆ TINH"). |
| 12 | Panel header — entity name | Heading | No event. Large display of the entity's name (e.g., "EARTH"). |
| 13 | Panel header — state badge | Badge | No event. Displays orbital data in a cyan accent chip (e.g., "Chu kỳ quỹ đạo 365 ngày · quỹ đạo đồng bộ JPL"). |
| 14 | Panel tab navigation (e.g., "TỔNG QUAN", "VẬT LÝ & QUỸ ĐẠO", "BẦU TRỜI & LỘ TRÌNH") | Tab Bar | Click a tab → Switches the panel content to the selected tab. Active tab is underlined with the accent colour. Tabs and labels are configured per entity in Studio. |
| 15 | Panel content blocks (PanelBlock) | Content Blocks | No event independently. Rendered inside each tab. Block types include: text (heading \+ paragraph), image (image with caption), and chart (horizontal bar chart with labelled data points). Block styles can be glass, solid, or minimal. Accent colour inherits from the active planet's CSS variable. |
| 16 | Satellite / sub-entity chips (e.g., "MOON", "ISS", "ARTEMIS I") | Chip Group | No event individually. Displayed under the entity group label. Lists related satellites or missions. Clicking may be configured per entity. |
| 17 | Concept chips ("Khái niệm trong bài") | Chip Group | No event. Up to 8 concept tags linked to the entity are displayed as rounded border chips, corresponding to learning concepts in the curriculum. |
| 18 | Gem gamification strip | Action Strip | Displayed at the bottom of the panel when gem-gated content exists. Shows the user's gem balance and unlock buttons. Click "Mở story · N gem" → Deducts gems and unlocks the narrative content block. Click "Mở orbit · N gem" → Deducts gems and unlocks the orbital data block. |
| 19 | Panel footer — lesson count | Informational Label | No event. Shows "N lessons in your path" linking this entity to the user's learning path. |
| 20 | Panel footer — "open in learning path →" link | Text Link | Click → Navigates to the first linked lesson in the learning path. |
| 21 | "KIỂM TRA NHANH" quiz prompt (ExploreBridgeQuiz) | Modal Overlay | Appears when the learning bridge triggers a quick quiz after the user dwells on an entity. Displays the entity name, a prompt message, multiple-choice questions, and a gem-reward notice (e.g., "+3 Gem nếu đúng hết"). Click "Bắt đầu" → Begins the quiz. Click "✕" → Dismisses the overlay. Answering questions updates the score and may award gems. |
| 22 | Cosmo AI assistant widget | Floating Button | Fixed at the bottom-right corner. Click → Opens the AI chat assistant pre-loaded with the current entity and scene context for contextual astronomy questions. |

5. # **IMPLEMENTATION AND TESTING** {#implementation-and-testing}

   1. ## **Link Github: [Link](https://github.com/quangg1/ASTRO_EDU)**  {#link-github:-link}

   2. ## **Development Implementation** {#development-implementation}

The development phase of the Cosmo Learn platform is built upon a modern distributed multi-service architecture, with a clear separation between the Frontend, the main Backend API, the Earth History Service, and the AI/Embedding Services. Technology choices were carefully made to ensure performance, scalability, cross-platform accessibility, and the best possible learning experience for users.

1. ### **Backend Implementation** {#backend-implementation}

The backend system plays a central role in handling business logic, data management, user authentication, and integration with external services. It is organized as a modular monolith deployed alongside independent specialized microservices. Key technologies used include:

* Runtime Environment: Node.js: Selected for its event-driven, non-blocking I/O model, which ensures high concurrency handling for simultaneous API requests such as course enrollment, lesson progress updates, and payment callbacks without degrading system performance.

* Framework: Express.js: A minimalist and flexible web framework for Node.js, used to implement a modular RESTful API organized into feature-based routers covering authentication, courses, community, payments, media upload, and administration.

* Database: MongoDB & Mongoose: Utilizes the NoSQL document database MongoDB for flexible and schema-free data storage, accommodating complex and evolving data structures such as lesson content blocks, learning paths, and geological stage data. Mongoose is used as an ODM (Object Data Modeling) library to define schemas, enforce validation rules, and interact with the database in a structured manner.

* Security:

  * JWT (JSON Web Token): Stateless authentication mechanism used to issue, verify, and manage user sessions across all protected API routes.

  * BCryptjs: Strong password hashing library used to securely hash and verify user passwords before storage, ensuring credentials are never persisted in plaintext.

  * Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Enforced via custom authMiddleware and requireRole() middleware, ensuring that each API route is accessible only by users with the appropriate role (student, teacher, moderator, or admin).

  * HMAC-SHA512 Signature Verification: Applied to all VNPay payment callback parameters to validate their authenticity before processing any enrollment or order status update.

* Feature Modules (modular monolith under `services/api/features/`):

  * **auth / users** — local register with email verification, JWT sessions, Firebase social login, teacher applications, profile and account lifecycle.

  * **courses / learning-path / concepts** — purchasable courses, platform learning path editor, shared concept library, progress, recall quiz, solar-journey milestones.

  * **content3d** — showcase entity CMS, JPL orbit cache, Earth History stages & fossils, planet narrative, Explore sky targets, contextual quiz pools.

  * **agent** — Cosmo assistant message pipeline (context build, quota, RAG proxy to Python AI, tool authorization, SSE streaming, session persistence).

  * **learning-state** — concept/lesson mastery events ingested from learning path and Explore for analytics and coach policy.

  * **rewards** — gem wallet, `rewardEngine`, shop catalog, avatar decorations, showcase unlock costs, admin gem-economy tuning.

  * **community / messages / notifications** — forums, news crawl, moderation queue, direct messages, inbox + WebSocket push (`/ws/notifications`).

  * **payment / promotions / admin** — VNPay checkout, promo codes, scoped admin routes (`adminScopes`), analytics aggregates, audit log, system jobs.

* External Integrations:

  * Firebase Admin SDK: Used to verify Firebase ID tokens returned from Google and Facebook OAuth social login flows, enabling secure third-party authentication without exposing provider credentials to the client.

  * VNPay Payment Gateway: Integrated for processing paid course transactions, constructing signed payment URLs, and securely handling callback verification upon transaction completion.

    2. ### **Earth History Service Implementation** {#earth-history-service-implementation}

Earth History and Explore 3D data are implemented as the **content3d** feature inside the main API (`/api/earth-history/*`, `/api/showcase-*`, `/api/explore/*`), while large fossil and stage datasets may use a dedicated MongoDB database (`earth_history`) separate from core platform collections (`galaxies`). Key aspects include:

* Fossil Data Management: Stores and serves over 500,000 fossil occurrence records sourced from the Paleobiology Database (PBDB), each containing geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude), taxonomic classification (phylum, class, order, genus), and geological time range (timeStart and timeEnd in millions of years ago). Records are indexed on time range fields to support fast time-filtered queries required by the real-time simulator.

* Geological Stage API: Provides endpoints for retrieving geological stage records, each containing a stage name, time boundaries, description, climate data, and a mapped Earth texture key that the 3D simulator uses to dynamically change the globe's appearance as the user navigates through geological time.

* Phylum Metadata API: Exposes phylum display metadata — including Vietnamese display names, descriptions, and color codes — enabling the frontend to render labeled and color-coded fossil point clusters on the 3D globe without additional lookups.

  3. ### **AI Service Implementation** {#ai-service-implementation}

The AI Service is developed using **Python FastAPI** and implements a full Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline to power the Cosmo Assistant AI Tutor. Key technologies and components include:

* Framework: FastAPI: A high-performance Python web framework with native support for asynchronous request handling, used to expose the AI chat endpoint and knowledge management endpoints with automatic request validation via Pydantic models.

* Embedding Model: BAAI/bge-m3: A state-of-the-art multilingual text embedding model deployed as a separate FastAPI service (port 5004). It generates high-dimensional vector representations of user queries and knowledge corpus chunks, supporting accurate semantic search on Vietnamese-language content without relying on language-specific preprocessing.

* RAG Pipeline:

  * Knowledge Corpus: The platform's curated astronomy and Earth science knowledge base is stored as Markdown files, parsed into chunks at index build time, and embedded into a vector index stored as a JSON file (rag\_index.json).

  * Cosine Similarity Retrieval: At query time, the user's embedded query is compared against the pre-built index using cosine similarity to retrieve the top-k most semantically relevant knowledge chunks, which are injected into the LLM's system prompt as grounding context.

  * Security Filtering: Every incoming user message is passed through a content blocklist (security.py) before reaching the LLM, preventing misuse for off-topic or inappropriate content.

* LLM Integration:

  * OpenRouter: Cloud-based LLM provider supporting multiple free and paid language models, used for production and internet-connected environments.

  * LM Studio: Locally hosted LLM backend used during development and offline environments, accessible via the same OpenAI-compatible API interface, ensuring the AI service can operate without external API dependencies.

  * Agent Tools (Function Calling): When enabled via the USE\_AGENT\_TOOLS environment flag, the LLM is provided with structured tool definitions — such as open\_lesson and go\_to\_explore — allowing it to return structured navigation actions alongside text responses. The client executes these actions to proactively guide users to relevant lessons or Earth History time periods based on the conversation.

  * Multimodal Support: The service accepts base64-encoded images alongside text queries, forwarding them to vision-capable LLM models to enable multimodal input processing for the AI Tutor.

* **Node.js Agent Orchestration** (API layer, UC-25): Before calling Python, `messagePipeline` enforces quiz-lock rules, message length caps, guest session resolution, entitlement tier, per-day quota, context budget trimming, RAG lesson id selection, optional ReAct tool loops, SSE token streaming, and persistence of `AgentSession` messages. Tool calls returned to the client are executed via `executeAgentClientAction` after `sanitizeAssistantContent`.

    4. ### **Frontend Implementation** {#frontend-implementation}

The user interface is designed to be immersive, visually engaging, and optimized for a consistent experience across both desktop browsers and mobile devices. Key technologies used include:

* Framework: Next.js 14 (App Router): The primary frontend framework, providing file-based routing, React Server Components for server-side rendering of public pages, and a hybrid rendering model that optimizes performance by minimizing unnecessary client-side JavaScript.

* Language: TypeScript: Used throughout the entire codebase to enforce static type safety, reduce runtime errors, and improve maintainability across a large component-based application.

* 3D Rendering: Three.js & React Three Fiber: Used to develop the platform's 3D simulation modules — including the Earth History globe, the Solar System scene, and the Milky Way visualization. React Three Fiber enables declarative composition of Three.js scenes using React components, integrating naturally with the application's component architecture.

* Styling: Tailwind CSS: A utility-first CSS framework used for rapid, consistent, and responsive UI construction throughout the application, combined with custom animations and glassmorphism-inspired design elements to achieve a premium visual aesthetic.

* State Management: Zustand: A lightweight global state management library used for authentication (`useAuthStore`), Earth History playback/stages (`useEarthHistoryStore`), planet narrative beats, and other focused domains — avoiding prop drilling in 3D-heavy routes.

* Feature-Oriented Client Modules: Business areas mirror the API — `features/agent` (Cosmo widget + `useCosmoAssistantChat`), `features/learning-path`, `features/content3d/showcase`, `features/explore`, `features/community`, `features/rewards`, `features/admin` — each exporting typed API clients and hooks.

* Explore 3D Composition (UC-21 / UC-22): `/explore` uses `useExplorePage` to compose mode/URL state (`useExploreModeState`), showcase catalog merge (NASA seed + CMS + JPL orbits), sky catalog (`useExploreSkyCatalog`), camera URL sync (`useExploreShowcaseNav`), learning bridge & contextual quiz (`useExploreLearningBridge`), and `ExploreSceneCanvas` switching between `ShowcaseScene`, `EarthScene`, `PlanetHistoryScene`, and `SkyPlanetariumScene`.

* API Integration: Each backend service is accessed through typed API client modules that centralize all HTTP requests and error handling, using NEXT\_PUBLIC\_\* environment variables to configure service base URLs for environment-specific deployments.

* Authentication: Firebase SDK: The Firebase JavaScript SDK is used on the client side to initiate Google and Facebook OAuth authentication flows, returning a Firebase ID token that is sent to the backend for verification and JWT issuance.

* Sequence Diagrams: Detailed interaction flows for product use cases UC-21–UC-50 are maintained as draw.io sources under `docs/diagrams/sequence/` (generated via `npm run diagrams:seq`), aligned with the business logic described in §5.4.

  3. ## **Deployment Implementation** {#deployment-implementation}

Link website: [**Cosmo Learn**](https://cosmo-learn-fr.onrender.com/)

The system deployment process of the Cosmo Learn platform is organized around its multi-service architecture, with each service deployed and managed independently to ensure modularity and ease of maintenance.

* Frontend Hosting: Vercel:

  * Chosen as the primary deployment platform due to its native compatibility with Next.js 14, providing built-in support for the App Router and React Server Components.

  * Provides global CDN infrastructure, ensuring fast content delivery to users regardless of geographic location.

* Backend Services: The Node.js/Express.js API services are deployed on a Node.js-compatible cloud server, while the two Python FastAPI services (AI Tutor and Embedding) are deployed on a separate Python-compatible environment, each running as independent processes.

* Database: MongoDB Atlas: Cloud-hosted MongoDB Atlas is used as the production database, providing managed infrastructure with automated backups and built-in security. Two separate databases are configured: galaxies for main platform data and earth\_history for geological and fossil records.

* CI/CD Integration:

  * Git Integration: The source code is managed on GitHub, with Vercel directly connected to the repository for automated deployments on every push to the main branch.

  * Preview Environments: Every Pull Request automatically generates an isolated preview deployment for testing before merging.

  4. ## **Business Logic Implementation** {#business-logic-implementation}

     1. ### **Course Enrollment & Payment Flow** {#course-enrollment-&-payment-flow}

To ensure a secure enrollment experience, the system implements a structured payment verification mechanism when a student purchases a paid course:

* Payment URL Generation: The system creates a pending Order record and generates a signed VNPay payment URL using HMAC-SHA512 hashing. The student is redirected to the VNPay gateway to complete the transaction.

* Callback Verification: Upon payment completion, the system re-computes the HMAC-SHA512 signature from the returned parameters. Only requests where the signatures match and vnp\_ResponseCode equals "00" are accepted as valid.

* Automatic Enrollment: Upon successful verification, the system updates the Order status to "completed" and automatically creates an Enrollment record, granting the student immediate access to the course content.

  2. ### **RAG-Based AI Tutor Pipeline** {#rag-based-ai-tutor-pipeline}

To provide accurate, domain-specific responses and minimize hallucination, the AI Tutor (UC-25) processes each user message through a **two-tier pipeline** — Node.js orchestration plus Python RAG/LLM:

* **Gatekeeping (API):** `assertAgentNotQuizLocked` blocks chat while a recall quiz is active; message length is capped (`AGENT_MAX_USER_MESSAGE_CHARS`); rate limits and per-tier **quota** apply before any LLM call.

* **Context assembly:** `stepBuildContext` merges session surface (learning path, course, explore), learner snapshot, entitlement tier, optional prefetch cache, and trimmed message history under a **context budget**. Concept quiz, spaced review, and coach nudge policies read the same learning-state signals.

* **Semantic Retrieval (Python):** The user utterance is embedded with BGE-M3 and matched against `rag_index.json` via cosine similarity; top-k chunks plus optional lesson-scoped RAG are injected into the system prompt.

* **Generation & tools:** FastAPI returns streamed tokens and optional `tool_calls`. The API may run a **ReAct loop** for server-side tools; client-executable tools (e.g. `open_lesson`, `go_to_explore`) are sanitized and dispatched by `executeAgentClientAction`.

* **Persistence:** Replies and tool metadata are stored on `AgentSession`; optional SSE (`event:token` … `event:done`) delivers partial text to `CosmoAssistantWidget`.

  3. ### **Earth History Simulator Data Loading** {#earth-history-simulator-data-loading}

To support smooth navigation across 4.6 billion years of geological time, the simulator implements an efficient on-demand data strategy:

* Stage-Based Rendering: As the user drags the timeline slider, the system dynamically swaps the globe's texture and climate parameters to match the selected geological stage without requiring a new server request.

* Time-Filtered Fossil Queries: Fossil records are loaded on-demand via a time-filtered API request, retrieving only records whose time range overlaps with the current stage and rendering them as color-coded instanced mesh points on the 3D globe.

  4. ### **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)** {#role-based-access-control-(rbac)}

To protect system resources across all user roles, the platform enforces a layered RBAC mechanism:

* API-Level Enforcement: Every protected route is guarded by authMiddleware (JWT validation) and requireRole() (role comparison). Requests failing either check are rejected before any business logic executes.

* Content Ownership Validation: For teacher-owned resources, the system verifies that the teacherId of the resource matches the authenticated user's ID before allowing any update or delete operation.

* **Admin scope matrix:** Beyond role, admins may hold granular `adminScopes` (users, orders, analytics, gem, broadcast, teachers). `requireAdminScope()` guards routes such as `/admin/analytics/*`, `/admin/gem-economy/*`, and `/admin/notifications/broadcast` so operators only access modules they are assigned.

  5. ### **Gem Economy & Learner Rewards** {#gem-economy-&-learner-rewards}

The gem system (UC-33, UC-34, UC-48) centralizes earn/spend rules in `rewardEngine` and admin-tunable runtime config:

* **Earn paths:** Lesson progress, recall quiz outcomes, Explore dwell milestones, community posts (daily-capped), onboarding steps, and admin manual adjustments all call `applyGemEarn`, which updates `UserReward.gemBalance`, writes `GemTransaction`, may trigger **level-up**, and runs learner-tier progression.

* **Spend paths:** Gem Shop purchases (`POST /api/gems/decorations/purchase`), showcase story/orbit unlocks (`POST /api/showcase/unlock`), and course vouchers debit balance after server-side price validation.

* **Caps & multipliers:** `GemRuntimeConfig` supplies seasonal multipliers and daily earn caps; `utcDayBounds` enforces per-calendar-day limits in community and explore rewards.

* **Admin economy (UC-48):** Operators view velocity metrics, patch runtime config, CRUD shop SKUs, and post manual adjustments — each logged in `GemEconomyAuditLog`.

  6. ### **Explore 3D, Showcase & Sky Planetarium** {#explore-3d-showcase-&-sky-planetarium}

Explore (UC-21, UC-22, UC-23 bridge) implements a single route with URL-driven modes:

* **Solar showcase:** Client merges bundled `NASA_SHOWCASE_ITEMS` with `GET /api/showcase-entities` CMS rows and `GET /api/showcase-orbits/jpl` vectors; `ShowcaseScene` renders orbits; entity picks sync `?entity=` and camera `?dist=&az=&el=`.

* **Earth deep history:** `?stage=` opens `EarthScene`; stages and time-filtered fossils load from `/api/earth-history`; globe texture and climate swap client-side on timeline scrub (no round-trip per frame).

* **Planet deep history:** `?history=1&entity=` loads narrative beats via `/api/planet-narrative/:entityId` into `PlanetHistoryScene`.

* **Sky planetarium:** `?view=sky` loads `GET /api/explore/sky-targets` (seed file + bundled fallback), merges western HIP catalog client-side, and computes ephemeris for the observer query (`lat`, `lon`, `time`).

* **Learning bridge:** After focus dwell, `useExploreLearningBridge` fetches `GET /api/explore/contextual-quiz/:entityId` (UC-23) and posts learning-state explore events; gem toasts listen on `learning-path-rewards`.

  7. ### **Learning Path, Progress & Quizzes** {#learning-path-progress-&-quizzes}

Platform curriculum (UC-08, UC-10, UC-15, UC-42) is stored as a single `LearningPath` document (`slug: main`):

* **Consumption:** Students traverse modules → nodes → depth tiers; `PUT /api/learning-path/progress` records section completion and may emit gem segments via `mergeRewardSegments`.

* **Recall quiz (UC-15):** Short retention quizzes gate Cosmo chat (`quizLock`) until passed; editor can auto-generate drafts via `POST /api/learning-path/editor/generate-quiz` (AI rate-limited).

* **Authoring (UC-42):** Teachers `GET/PUT /api/learning-path/editor`; server normalizes modules, validates concept ids against the UC-43 library, returns `invalidConceptIds` warnings, and schedules **RAG reindex** after save.

* **Solar journey (UC-35):** Milestone ids persist in localStorage for guests and sync through `GET/PUT /api/learning-path/solar-journey/progress` for signed-in learners.

  8. ### **Community, Moderation & Messaging** {#community-moderation-&-messaging}

Community features (UC-28–UC-32) enforce access and auditability:

* **Browse & post:** Forums list via `postListQuery`; news uses a separate crawl-backed channel. Creating posts runs `assertCohortForumAccess` for cohort forums, rejects news forum posts, merges auto-tags, and may award first-post-of-day gems.

* **Report & moderate (UC-30, UC-31):** Students `POST /api/community/moderation/reports`; moderators consume `GET /moderation/queue`, then hide content, resolve reports, or `POST /moderation/warn` (creates `UserWarning` + notification).

* **Direct messages (UC-32):** `GET /api/messages/conversations`, `POST /open`, `GET /conversations/:id`, `POST /send` via `dmService`; recipients may receive real-time notification over `/ws/notifications`.

  9. ### **Admin Operations, Analytics & Broadcast** {#admin-operations-analytics-&-broadcast}

Admin workflows (UC-45–UC-50) combine scoped APIs and Mongo aggregates:

* **Users & teachers (UC-45, UC-47):** Search/paginate users, patch role/status/scopes, send password reset, review `teacher-applications` with applicant notifications.

* **Orders (UC-46):** `adminOrderService` lists/filters orders, supports admin notes, cancel pending, refund completed (revokes enrollments) — each action recorded in `AdminActionLog`.

* **Promo & broadcast (UC-49):** CRUD promo codes; broadcast creates bulk `Notification` rows for role-filtered users.

* **Analytics (UC-50):** Dashboard tabs call `/admin/analytics/overview`, `/funnel`, `/learning-path`, `/explore` — all **MongoDB aggregates** (not GA API). Client GA4 (`gtag`) is optional telemetry only. Audit and system pages expose action logs and job health (e.g. news crawl trigger).

  5. ## **System Testing** {#system-testing}

     1. ### **Purpose** {#purpose}

The primary purpose of System Testing is to validate the complete and integrated software product to ensure it meets the specified requirements. This phase aims to:

* Verify that all system components (Frontend, Backend API, Earth History Service, AI Service, and Database) interact correctly across the full request-response lifecycle.

* Validate that the system functions as expected from the end-user's perspective across all four user roles: student, teacher, moderator, and administrator.

* Identify and resolve bugs, logic errors, and edge cases before the final submission and demonstration.

* Ensure the system is secure, stable, and performs reliably under expected usage conditions, including 3D rendering, AI chat interactions, and payment processing.

  2. ### **Overview** {#overview}

* Test Strategy: The testing approach combines both functional and manual testing methodologies.

  * Functional API Testing: Applied for all backend API endpoints using Postman to verify authentication enforcement, request validation, data processing, and response structure correctness.

  * Manual Testing: Extensively used for the Frontend UI/UX, user flows across all roles, 3D simulation interactions, AI Tutor conversations, and payment checkout to ensure a natural and user-friendly experience.

* Execution Strategy: Testing is performed in multiple environments:

  * Local Environment: Each service is run and tested individually during implementation to verify feature correctness in isolation.

  * Integration Environment: All five services are run simultaneously to verify cross-service interactions such as AI Tutor responses, VNPay payment callbacks, and Earth History data loading.

  * Device Environment: The PWA and Android APK are tested on physical devices and multiple browsers to verify cross-platform compatibility.

* Test Management: Test cases and bug reports are tracked using GitHub Issues to record identified defects, assign fixes, and monitor resolution status throughout the development cycle.

  3. ### **Techniques** {#techniques}

The project employs a multi-level testing approach:

* Unit Testing:

  * Focuses on testing individual components or functions in isolation.

  * Tools: Manual checks for Node.js utility functions (e.g., input validation helpers, JWT generation), and component-level inspection for React UI components.

* Integration Testing:

  * Verifies the interfaces and interactions between different modules (e.g., Frontend calling Backend APIs, Backend querying MongoDB, AI service calling the Embedding service).

  * Tools: Postman (for API endpoint testing), browser DevTools Network tab (for client-server integration verification).

* Regression Testing:

  * Performed after every significant code change or new feature addition to ensure that existing functionalities are not broken.

  * Approach: Re-running critical test cases and key user flows (authentication, enrollment, lesson viewing, AI chat, payment) after each development iteration.

* Acceptance Testing (UAT): The final phase where the software is tested for acceptability. The goal is to evaluate the system's compliance with the defined functional requirements and assess whether it is ready for demonstration and delivery.

  4. ### **Test Scope** {#test-scope}

| Role | Function | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Guest | Authentication | Register a new account, log in with email/password, log in with Google/Facebook, reset forgotten password. |
|  | Course Discovery | Browse and search course catalog, view course details. |
| Student | Learning | Enroll in free courses, purchase paid courses via VNPay, view lesson content (text/video/3D), take quizzes, track learning progress. |
|  | AI Tutor | Chat with AI Cosmo Assistant using text and image input, receive agent-triggered navigation to lessons and simulator. |
|  | 3D Simulation | Solar showcase orbits, Earth/planet deep history, sky planetarium, contextual quiz bridge, solar-journey milestones. |
|  | Community | Browse forums/news, create posts and comments, report content, direct messages. |
|  | Rewards | Earn/spend gems, gem shop & avatar decorations, showcase unlocks. |
|  | Account | Update profile, change password, view order history, notifications inbox. |
| Teacher | Studio | Create and edit courses, manage modules and lessons, design quizzes, upload media, manage learning paths and tutorials. |
|  | Analytics | View course enrollment statistics and lesson completion rates. |
| Moderator | Moderation | View violation report queue, hide violating posts, send warnings to users. |
| Admin | User Management | Search users, change roles/scopes, deactivate and restore accounts, password reset. |
|  | Teacher Approval | Review, approve, and reject teacher registration applications. |
|  | Financial | View and manage payment orders (note, refund, cancel), promo codes, gem economy config. |
|  | System | Mongo-backed analytics dashboard, audit log, system status, broadcast notifications. |

6. # **CONCLUSION** {#conclusion}

   1. ## **Achieved Results** {#achieved-results}

After the research and development process, the Cosmo Learn (ASTRO\_EDU) project has been successfully completed, meeting the initial requirements and objectives. The key achievements include:

* Comprehensive System Architecture: Successfully designed and implemented a distributed multi-service architecture that cleanly separates the Frontend, Main Backend API, Earth History Service, and AI/Embedding Services. This ensures the system is modular, independently scalable, and maintainable across all components.

* Functional Completeness: The platform provides a full range of features for all defined user roles:

  * Students: Can browse and enroll in courses, access rich multimedia lesson content, take quizzes, track learning progress, explore 3D scientific simulations, chat with the AI Tutor, and participate in the community forum.

  * Teachers: Have powerful tools through the Studio interface to create and publish courses, design lessons using a block-based editor, manage learning paths, and view course analytics.

  * Moderators: Can review violation reports, hide inappropriate community content, and send warnings to users.

  * Administrators: Can monitor the entire platform through an analytics dashboard, manage user accounts and roles, approve teacher applications, and oversee financial transactions.

* Advanced Technology Integration:

  * AI Tutor (RAG Pipeline): Integrated a context-aware AI assistant powered by Retrieval-Augmented Generation, capable of answering domain-specific astronomy and Earth science questions in Vietnamese, processing image inputs, and proactively navigating users to relevant content through agent function calling.

  * 3D Scientific Simulations: Successfully developed an Earth History Simulator featuring a real-time animated globe, a geological timeline spanning 4.6 billion years, and geographically distributed fossil occurrence data from over 500,000 PBDB records — alongside a Solar System scene and Milky Way visualization.

  * VNPay Payment Integration: Implemented a complete course purchase flow with HMAC-SHA512 signature verification and automatic enrollment granting upon payment confirmation.

* Modern User Experience: The interface is built with Next.js 14 and Tailwind CSS, offering a visually immersive, responsive, and fast experience across desktop browsers, with an astronomy-themed dark design aesthetic that enhances learner engagement.

  2. ## **Future Development** {#future-development}

To further enhance the platform and meet the growing demands of interactive science education, the following development directions are proposed:

* iOS Application Development: Extend the Capacitor-based mobile application to support iOS, enabling learners on Apple devices to access the full platform experience natively on iPhone and iPad.

* Advanced AI Capabilities:

  * Personalized Learning Recommendations: Integrate a recommendation engine that analyzes each student's learning history and progress to proactively suggest relevant courses, tutorials, and learning paths tailored to their interests and knowledge gaps.

  * Voice Interaction: Enable voice-to-text input for the AI Tutor, allowing learners to ask questions hands-free — particularly useful during 3D simulation exploration where both hands may be occupied with navigation.

* Gamification Expansion: Fully develop the Gem Economy system with a complete Learner Tier ranking mechanism, daily challenge rewards, achievement badges, and a seasonal Gem Shop, increasing long-term learner engagement and motivation.

* Real-Time Collaboration Features: Implement WebSocket-based real-time features such as live cohort study sessions, collaborative annotation on lesson content, and real-time discussion threads linked directly to specific lesson sections.
